Florida confirms the DMV data breach

FLHSMV says its investigation traced the breach to credentials belonging to a single Plant City Police Department user. According to the agency, those credentials were improperly stored on the employee's personal electronic device. A criminal actor was then able to take advantage of them.
That explanation gives us the first official account of how the breach occurred. It also differs from the access method ShinyHunters previously described.

FLHSMV says it notified the Florida Office of the Attorney General as required under state law. The agency is also working with the Florida Digital Service and Florida Department of Law Enforcement. The criminal investigation remains ongoing. Officials say additional information will be released at an appropriate time.
What ShinyHunters claims it stole from Florida

ShinyHunters says it stole more than 200,000 driver records from DAVID. BleepingComputer reported that the group provided a screenshot of a DAVID record belonging to Jeffrey Epstein as evidence that it had accessed the system. The screenshot reportedly contained an address, Social Security number, birth date, driver's license information and registered vehicle details.

DAVID can contain far more than a person's basic driver's license information. Government records describing the system show that authorized users may have access to driver information, photographs, signatures, vehicle history, insurance information and other identifying records.
However, FLHSMV still has not disclosed how many records were accessed or stolen. The agency also has not confirmed ShinyHunters' claim that more than 200,000 records were taken.
CyberGuy reached out to FLHSMV for additional comment, but did not hear back before our deadline.
Florida's findings conflict with the hackers' password-reset claim

ShinyHunters originally told BleepingComputer that it breached DAVID through a password-reset flaw. The group claimed that weakness allowed it to compromise multiple accounts, allegedly including accounts belonging to DMV employees and an FBI agent. ShinyHunters said it then moved through DAVID record IDs and downloaded associated pages and driver files beginning Sept. 3. The group later said it had lost access and believed the password-reset issue was being patched.

Florida's investigation now points somewhere else. FLHSMV says the attacker took advantage of credentials belonging to one Plant City Police Department user that had been improperly stored on a personal electronic device. The agency has not backed ShinyHunters' claim that a password-reset flaw allowed the group to compromise multiple accounts. So, for now, the password-reset explanation remains ShinyHunters' version of events, while compromised police credentials are the access method Florida has publicly identified.
Why Florida's DAVID database holds sensitive information

DAVID serves authorized government users rather than ordinary public searches. FLHSMV says its Bureau of Records manages access to driver records through DAVID for law enforcement and other approved entities. The agency also audits users for compliance.

Florida policy treats personal information in motor vehicle records as confidential. That information can include Social Security numbers, driver identification numbers, addresses and medical or disability information. That kind of information can give criminals powerful material for identity theft.

Imagine getting a call from someone claiming to represent a government agency. The caller already knows your address, birth date and driver's license information. Suddenly, the scam sounds far more convincing.
IS YOUR SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER ON THE DARK WEB?
Florida’s DAVID system gives law enforcement and other approved users access to driver and vehicle records. (Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles)
ShinyHunters claims other state DMV systems are being targeted

BleepingComputer previously reported that a source said the attackers were targeting DMV platforms in other states through social engineering. ShinyHunters also told the outlet it expected additional DMV breaches to surface.

There has been no confirmation from Florida that the current breach involved other state DMV systems. Still, the possibility deserves attention because state motor vehicle agencies hold information that can be extremely valuable for identity fraud and targeted scams.
If criminals find a technique that works against one government system, they often look for similar access elsewhere.
Who is ShinyHunters?
ShinyHunters is an extortion operation associated with data theft attacks against companies and online services.
Threat actors using the name have been linked to attacks involving Salesforce environments and companies including Google, Cisco and Match Group.

More recently, the attackers have used voice phishing, also called vishing. In these attacks, someone impersonates IT support and tries to convince an employee to enter credentials or authentication codes into a phishing site.
The attackers have also targeted single sign-on accounts connected to services such as Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and Salesforce.

FLHSMV referred to the attacker in its statement only as an "international cybercriminal organization." The agency did not publicly identify ShinyHunters by name. So, while ShinyHunters has claimed responsibility and Florida has confirmed a breach, Florida has not publicly attributed the attack to the group.
Still, this shows why protecting trusted accounts has become so important. Once an attacker gets legitimate credentials, other connected services may become accessible too.
8 ways to stay safe if your DMV data may be exposed
You do not need to wait for a confirmed case of identity theft before protecting yourself. These steps can make stolen personal information harder for criminals to use.

A credit freeze can make it harder for someone to open new credit accounts in your name. You need to place a freeze separately with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. Credit freezes are free. You can temporarily lift one when you legitimately need a lender to access your credit.

Check your credit reports for new accounts or inquiries you do not recognize. You can request your reports through AnnualCreditReport.com, the federally authorized source for free credit reports. Also, keep an eye on your financial accounts. Small unfamiliar transactions can sometimes be an early warning sign.

A confirmed breach creates a ready-made lure for scammers. You could receive a text, email or phone call claiming your Florida driver information was exposed. Be especially careful if the sender pressures you to verify personal information or click a link. Instead, visit FLHSMV through its official website at flhsmv.gov/ yourself.
FAKE SHINYHUNTERS SEXTORTION EMAIL USES CARNIVAL BREACH DATA
Florida officials confirmed a breach of the state’s DMV database after hackers claimed they stole more than 200,000 driver records. (Nikolas Kokovlis/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Scammers may use news of a DMV breach to send fake alerts containing malicious links or attachments. Strong antivirus software can help detect malware, phishing sites and other threats before they compromise your device or personal information. Keep your antivirus software running and updated on your computers and mobile devices. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com

Your primary email account deserves extra attention because criminals can use it to reset passwords for other services. Give it a strong, unique password and use a password manager to create and securely store it. Then turn on multifactor authentication. Whenever possible, consider an authenticator app or passkey rather than relying only on codes sent by text message.

Review bank accounts, credit cards and other important services for activity you do not recognize. Also pay attention to unexpected government correspondence. A strange tax notice or benefits letter could signal that someone has used your identity.

You may also want to consider an identity theft protection service that monitors for suspicious use of your personal information and can help with recovery if your identity is stolen. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com
If you discover identity theft, report it at IdentityTheft.gov and follow the recovery steps provided by the Federal Trade Commission.

Data brokers and people-search websites can provide scammers with even more information about you. Removing that data cannot erase records stolen during a breach. However, reducing the information available elsewhere can make it harder for criminals to build a detailed profile and create convincing scams.

Consider using a personal data removal service to help find your information on data broker sites and submit removal requests on your behalf. These services can also keep checking for information that reappears over time. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting Cyberguy.com

Now that FLHSMV has confirmed the breach, scammers could imitate any future notices sent to affected drivers. FLHSMV has not yet publicly disclosed how many people were affected or exactly what information was taken. Do not automatically trust an email simply because it mentions DAVID or the Florida DMV. Avoid using links in unexpected messages. Go directly to the agency's official website to verify any notice.
Kurt's key takeaways

Florida has now confirmed the breach, but some of the biggest questions remain unanswered. ShinyHunters claims it stole more than 200,000 driver records, while Florida says the attacker got in using credentials belonging to a Plant City Police Department user that were improperly stored on a personal device. What we still do not know is exactly how much information was taken or whose records were exposed. Until Florida releases more details, I would take this seriously. Check your credit, lock down your important accounts and be especially suspicious of unexpected DMV texts, emails or calls asking you to verify personal information.

If hackers stole your driver's license record, Social Security number and address from a government database, how quickly would you expect the state to tell you? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

title: Tesla Cybercab bars kids under 13 as scrutiny grows
summary: Tesla's Cybercab launched in Austin with no steering wheel or pedals, but hidden details about age limits and missing safety features may shock riders.
story: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is scrutinizing robotaxi safety, documenting multiple instances of autonomous vehicles driving into active emergency scenes and blocking first responders. NHTSA states an AV that cannot safely interact with first responders poses a danger to the public. They will meet with robotaxi developers this month to discuss solutions.
Tesla's Cybercab is finally carrying riders in Austin, Texas. And some of the details buried in the fine print may surprise you.
The gold two-seater has no steering wheel or pedals. Tesla says it uses cameras and AI to handle the driving, putting passengers entirely in the hands of its autonomous system.

Yet the Sept. 3 launch was unusually low-key for Tesla. The main presentation reportedly lasted about 15 minutes, and Elon Musk apparently did not speak. Then, on Sept. 4, federal safety regulators announced an investigation into how Tesla certified Cybercab for U.S. roads.

Tesla has spent years building toward this moment. Now that real riders are climbing inside, the little details suddenly become much more important. Here is what you should know before you step into a Cybercab.
ZOOX ROBOTAXI REDESIGN BRINGS BIG RIDER UPGRADES

Tesla’s Cybercab is rolling onto Austin streets as the company expands its robotaxi push, even as new rider rules and safety questions draw attention. (Aaron E. Martinez/The Austin American-Statesman via Getty Images)
NEW! Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI

In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you take a more active role in your healthcare. You’ll learn how to organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare questions for your next doctor’s visit. No technical
experience is needed.
Register for free now at CyberGuyLive.com
Tesla Cybercab has a surprising age limit

If you planned to call a Cybercab for a family ride, check the passenger rules first. Tesla says children under 13 cannot ride in Cybercab "at this time." Teens ages 13 through 17 can ride, although an adult must accompany them for the entire trip.
Interestingly, Tesla sets a different age limit for the Model Y vehicles in its Robotaxi service. Children ages 8 through 17 can ride in those vehicles with an adult. Guests under 8 cannot.

So, an 11-year-old could ride in a Tesla Model Y Robotaxi but could not take the same trip in a Cybercab. Tesla does not explain the reason for that difference in its current rider guidance. Then there is another detail parents may notice.
Cybercab has no LATCH child-seat anchors
Tesla confirms that Cybercab has no LATCH or ISOFIX child-restraint system. If a rider needs a booster seat, Tesla says it must use a seat belt to secure it.
That may sound odd considering Cybercab does not allow children under 13. However, some older children may still need a booster seat depending on their size and local requirements.
Tesla gives instructions for using one, but there are no LATCH anchors to attach it to. It is the kind of detail most of us probably would not think about until a Cybercab showed up at the curb.
What happens if a Cybercab crashes?

A driverless vehicle still needs a plan for the moment something goes wrong. According to Tesla documentation, a collision can trigger several automatic responses. The airbags can deploy and the doors can unlock. Hazard lights and interior lights can also switch on.

The vehicle can disable its high-voltage battery, move the windows into a vent position and apply the brakes until it comes to a stop. Tesla's system can also open a two-way connection with its Robotaxi Support team.
That support connection could become especially important in a vehicle where nobody can grab the steering wheel or hit the brakes. Tesla also gives riders ways to stop a trip themselves.
UBER LETS PARENTS WATCH TEEN RIDES LIVE
Tesla’s newest robotaxi introduces unique safety features, strict rider requirements and a federal review as autonomous service expands in Austin, Texas. (Ronaldo Schemidt/AFP via Getty Images)
There is an emergency Stop button

Look above you when you get inside a Cybercab. Tesla placed a dedicated Stop button between the dome lights. Pressing it sends an immediate pull-over request, ends the ride and connects you with Robotaxi Support.

You can also tap Pull Over on the touchscreen or make the request through the Robotaxi app. However, Tesla warns that an "immediate" pull-over may still take some time. For example, the vehicle may need longer to reach a safe stopping point while traveling on a highway. That is worth knowing before your first ride.
Tesla made the manual door release easier to find
Tesla's electronic door releases have attracted criticism because passengers may need a mechanical backup when a vehicle loses power.
Cybercab still uses electronically controlled doors during normal operation. In fact, the nearest door can open automatically when the ride requester approaches.

Inside, you can normally open the door through the touchscreen or gently lift a lever on the door panel. Pull that lever firmly all the way up, though, and it activates the mechanical release. Both Cybercab doors have one.

I like that Tesla put the emergency release where a passenger can actually see and reach it. There is one important warning. Tesla says using the mechanical release can damage the window or trim. If the vehicle has no power and the window remains fully raised, Tesla warns the glass could shatter when someone activates the release. That is one instruction I would want to know before an emergency.
Cybercab uses electronic braking

Tesla also made a major change underneath the vehicle. Cybercab uses a brake-by-wire system rather than a traditional hydraulic setup. Electronic actuators control the brake calipers instead of hydraulic lines carrying brake fluid.
Musk said in a post on X that electric brakes avoid the complexity of routing hydraulic plumbing around the vehicle. Tesla has already used steer-by-wire technology in the Cybertruck.
With Cybercab, passengers have no physical driving controls at all. That puts even more responsibility on the electronics and software to work properly every time.
Cybercab windows will not open all the way

Here is one of the stranger details Tesla included in its new rider guide. Cybercab passengers can lower the windows, but Tesla says they "cannot be fully opened at this time." The company does not explain why.
The window switches also sit underneath the center touchscreen rather than on the doors. So, yes, you can crack a window for some air. You simply cannot roll it all the way down right now.
WAYMO RECALLS ROBOTAXIS OVER CONSTRUCTION-ZONE RISK

Tesla’s driverless Cybercab enters commercial service as federal regulators review how the company certified the vehicle for U.S. roads. (Aaron E. Martinez/The Austin American-Statesman via Getty Images)
Cybercab packs USB-C charging
At least you should have somewhere to plug in your devices. Tesla confirms that Cybercab has USB-C charging ports inside the cabin.
An attendee at the launch reported that those ports can deliver up to 90 watts of power. That could be enough to charge many laptops.
However, Tesla's current public rider guide does not list that wattage. So, I would treat the 90-watt figure as an early report until Tesla publishes the specification itself.
Federal regulators are already looking at Cybercab

On Sept. 3, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened what it calls an Audit Query into Tesla's certification that Cybercab meets all applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. NHTSA announced the action on Sept. 4 following the vehicle's commercial deployment in Austin.
Automakers in the U.S. generally certify their own vehicles as complying with federal standards. NHTSA can then audit those certifications and investigate when questions come up.

Cybercab presents an unusual case because it has no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors. Many federal vehicle rules were written around cars designed for human drivers. NHTSA's audit reportedly covers about 1,000 Cybercabs as the agency reviews how Tesla determined the vehicles comply.
That does not mean regulators have found Cybercab unsafe. It does mean Tesla now has to back up its certification with technical information that satisfies the agency.
What this means to you

If you get the chance to ride in a Cybercab, I would spend a minute learning the cabin before the car starts moving. Find the emergency Stop button. Know where the mechanical door release sits. Keep your seat belt fastened for the entire trip.

Tesla says every passenger must buckle up before the ride begins. Cybercab may pull over or cancel a trip if it detects improper seat-belt use. Parents should also pay close attention to the age rules. Cybercab and Tesla's Model Y Robotaxi do not follow the same limits.

Beyond that, remember how new this vehicle is. Tesla is putting a very different kind of car into real-world service, and regulators are already asking questions about how it fits existing safety standards.

We have seen how unexpected situations can challenge other autonomous vehicles too. CyberGuy recently reported how Waymo recalled robotaxis over a construction-zone risk after vehicles entered closed freeway construction areas.
The technology can be impressive. Still, the real test comes when these vehicles deal with everything ordinary roads throw at them.
Kurt's key takeaways

Cybercab is finally moving from Tesla's big promise to something people can actually ride in. I like seeing safeguards such as the mechanical door release and emergency Stop button, especially when passengers have no steering wheel or pedals to grab. Still, the under-13 restriction, lack of LATCH anchors and windows that do not fully open caught my attention. Add the federal investigation, and Tesla now has something bigger to prove. Putting Cybercab on the road is one thing. Showing that people can trust it day after day is the real test.
Would you climb into a Cybercab today with no steering wheel or pedals, or would you want to see a longer safety record before trusting it with your ride? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

NEW JERSEY MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING WIFE WITH BARBELL ALLEGEDLY CONFESSED IN MESSAGES TO RELATIVES: REPORT

MICROSOFT EXEC'S GRIEVING WIDOW FACES MAN ACCUSED OF PLOTTING HIS MURDER AS SHE REVEALS EERIE FINAL CALL

title: Tourists seeking 'dramatic' photo on isolated beach trapped by incoming tide
summary: Drone footage captures three tourists spelling out "SOS" on Oregon's Lost Boy Beach after a rising tide trapped them in the Tillamook County cove.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Tourists went to snap an iconic photo on Oregon's Lost Boy Beach and wound up getting one taken of themselves in a storybook SOS rescue by the local fire department last week.

Three unnamed sea gawkers were stranded for five hours Wednesday, Sept. 16, after a rising tide cut them off from the mainland at the secluded Tillamook County cove. Having reportedly lost cell phone service at the bottom of the steep cliff, the group managed to contact 911 using an emergence satellite feature, The Oregonian reported.

Netarts-Oceanside Fire District received the call and found them stranded on the shrinking patch of beach with the tide rolling in on them, using a drone to capture footage of them spelling out a large "SOS" with sticks.
11 VISITORS TRAPPED AS DANGEROUS FLASH FLOODING TEARS THROUGH ICONIC NATIONAL PARK

Stranded thrill-seekers were discovered by local rescue workers on Lost Boy Beach in Oregon, spelling out SOS with dead sticks in footage captured by an emergency drone. (Netarts-Oceanside Fire District)

Lost Boy Beach is accessible only by scrambling over rocky terrain and passing through a sea cave that is open at both ends. While the small beach is inviting during low tide, the rising water blocks the only exit.
"When people are stranded there, we may not be able to get to them," NOFD Chief Jeff McBrayer told the paper.
HELICOPTER RESCUE CREW CAUGHT ON CAMERA SAVING 2 CLIMBERS TRAPPED ALONG POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH CLIFF

Three unnamed tourists were stranded on Lost Boy Beach in Oregon after trekking down a cliff to get what they called a 'dramatic' photo of an icon seascape. They wound up getting drone photos taken of their own rescue. (Netarts-Oceanside Fire District)

Crews initially considered waiting for the tide to recede, but opted for an active rescue due to rough surf, the presence of sneaker waves, and the fact that the tourists were already wet and cold, he added.

Navigating the dangerous conditions, rescuers hugged the remaining shoreline while secured to ropes instead of wading directly through the unpredictable water. Once they reached the tourists, responders provided life vests, clipped the group to the safety ropes, and guided them through the surf to a secure area where they could walk out on their own.
CALIFORNIA DAD PARALYZED FROM NECK DOWN AFTER DIVING INTO OCEAN TO RESCUE CHILD

The Netarts-Oceanside Fire District was able to rescue three thrill-seeking tourists who were stranded and wrote SOS with nearby sticks and issued a future warning about repeating their mistake. (Netarts-Oceanside Fire District)
The visitors emerged from the ordeal with only minor bumps and bruises.
Following the rescue, Chief McBrayer used the incident to remind coastal visitors of the area's deceptive dangers of exploring isolated coves.
"You have to ask a local or check a tide app on a phone for tide information," he said.
HIKERS STRANDED ON MOUNT SHASTA AFTER RELYING ON AI TO PLAN TRIP, SHERIFF SAYS

Drone footage captured the stranded sea gawkers after an emergency 911 signal sent from the location that was cut off from regular cell phone service, according to the report. (Netarts-Oceanside Fire District)

Lost Boy Beach, situated on the northern Oregon coast just south of a towering basalt cliff, derives its ominous name from a century-old local legend. According to regional lore, the highly secluded spot was named after a young boy who was believed to have drowned after being trapped by the incoming tide. While it remains unverified if the tragic tale is historically accurate, the name has persisted for roughly 100 years, functioning as a built-in, enduring warning to visitors about the cove's unpredictable and deadly conditions.

Historically, reaching this hidden stretch of sand has remained notoriously treacherous, wedged between Short Beach to the north and Tunnel Beach — sometimes known as Star Trek Beach — to the south. Unlike its neighboring Short Beach, which finally received a community-built "stairway of 100 steps" around 2000 to stop visitors from cracking their heads on a slippery cliff face, Lost Boy Beach has never featured safe overland access.

Navigating to the beach from either side is exceptionally dangerous, with access only vaguely possible during rare, extreme low-tide events that occur just a couple of times a year.

title: Attorney busts ‘biggest misconception’ in Karmelo Anthony filing that could be key in track meet murder case
summary: Karmelo Anthony's 75-page filing of alleged threats, gun photos and violent texts may never have reached jurors, a Texas defense attorney says.
story: Former prosecutor Tiffany Burks breaks down Rule 404(b) and why jurors were never guaranteed to see the allegations inside in the track meet murder case.

A 75-page court filing detailing alleged threats, gun photos and violent text messages tied to convicted Texas killer Karmelo Anthony appears at first glance to be a roadmap of evidence prosecutors planned to present at trial.
But a veteran Texas criminal defense attorney says one of the biggest misconceptions surrounding the document is that jurors were never guaranteed to see any of it.
Fox News Digital recently obtained the filing, which prosecutors submitted before Anthony's murder trial under Texas Rule of Evidence 404(b).
UNTAPPED KARMELO ANTHONY EVIDENCE CACHE SHOWED HE STALKED EX-GIRLFRIEND, HAD 'KNIVES' OBSESSION: PROSECUTORS

The filing has taken on renewed importance because Anthony's bid for a new trial focuses on an alleged pretrial agreement governing character evidence. Anthony argues confusion over that agreement affected his decision not to testify, while prosecutors dispute that claim.
Karmelo Anthony mugshot and photo of him holding a gun. (Texas Department of Corrections ; Credit: Collin County court records obtained by Fox News Digital)

The notice catalogs dozens of alleged prior acts prosecutors said they may seek to introduce, including allegations that Anthony stalked his girlfriend hours before fatally stabbing 17-year-old Austin Metcalf at a Frisco high school track meet on April 2, 2025.
Prosecutors also cited text messages in which Anthony allegedly said he was "on the verge," posed with firearms, made violent threats and repeatedly discussed fighting.
KARMELO ANTHONY PHOTOGRAPHED WITH GUNS AS DOCS REVEAL ALLEGED HISTORY OF RAGE, THREATS AND VIOLENCE

The filing also includes allegations that Anthony talked about committing robberies, buying firearms and extended magazines, selling narcotics and threatening multiple people, including his then-girlfriend, in text messages spanning several years. Prosecutors also cited screenshots they said represent only portions of larger conversations and noted the alleged prior acts were separate from the charged offense.
To some readers, the filing might appear to be a blueprint of the prosecution's case.
KARMELO ANTHONY DEFENSE RESTS, ATTORNEYS PREP FOR CLOSING ARGUMENTS BEFORE JURY DELIBERATES IN MURDER TRIAL
But appearances can be misleading.
Tiffany Burks, a partner at Texas law firm Varghese Summersett and a former prosecutor, said that's not how Rule 404(b) works.
TEXAS JUDGE WHO PRESIDED OVER KARMELO ANTHONY MURDER TRIAL REMOVED FROM CASE OVER 'GOT IT RIGHT' COMMENT

Burks explained that filing a Rule 404(b) notice does not mean jurors will ultimately hear the evidence. Instead, it gives the defense advance notice of evidence prosecutors may seek to introduce, so attorneys have time to investigate the allegations and prepare a response before trial.
KARMELO ANTHONY BLASTS JUDGE IN NEW FILING OVER HANDLING OF MURDER TRIAL

If prosecutors believe they may want to introduce evidence of prior alleged bad acts, they must notify the defense before trial, so attorneys have an opportunity to investigate the allegations, prepare a response and avoid being surprised before a jury.

Supporters of Karmelo Anthony assemble outside of Collin County Courthouse in McKinney, TX, on Wednesday, Aug. 19, 2026. Anthony was convicted of the murder of Austin Metcalf in June. (Derek Shook for Fox News Digital)

"The law requires that you file a 404(b) notice so that you can give the other side notice of what it is you may want to put in trial because the parties have to be prepared," Burks said. "Specifically, the defense has to be prepared to respond or rebut that information."
KARMELO ANTHONY ISOLATED IN JAIL AS TRACK MEET KILLER APPEALS CONVICTION, PREPS FOR PRISON STINT

In effect, the filing functioned as a placeholder, preserving prosecutors' ability to ask the judge to admit the evidence later if they believed it became relevant during trial. Filing the notice did not mean the judge would allow jurors to hear it, nor did it mean prosecutors would ultimately decide to offer every allegation listed in the document.
That also helps explain why Anthony's filing stretched to 75 pages.
CONVICTED KILLER KARMELO ANTHONY SENTENCED TO 35 YEARS AFTER YEARLONG LEGAL BATTLE: TIMELINE

Rule 404(b) generally prohibits prosecutors from introducing prior acts simply to argue a defendant has a bad character. But judges may admit that evidence for other purposes if it satisfies the rules of evidence.
Austin Metcalf, left, is pictured with his father, Jeff, top right, and with his twin brother, Hunter, bottom right. (Jeff Metcalf)

"When I was a prosecutor, I would put everything but the kitchen sink in the notice," Burks said. "If you don't give the other side notice of it, then you're not going to be able to utilize it later."
AUSTIN METCALF'S FATHER HAUNTED BY KARMELO ANTHONY TRIAL VISUALS RELEASED: ‘I HAD NEVER SEEN THOSE PICTURES’

The filing reaches back to Anthony's school years in Louisiana and includes allegations of repeated fights, school suspensions, threats, assaults and misconduct. It also cites text messages in which Anthony allegedly wrote, "When I get mad i see red," "When I get mad i blackout" and "When I get mad i cant control myself."

A screenshot cited in a Texas court filing shows messages attributed to Karmelo Anthony describing how he reacts when angry on Dec. 23, 2023. (Credit: Collin County Court records obtained by Fox News Digital)

After reviewing the filing following the trial, Metcalf's father, Jeff Metcalf, said he had "no idea" many of the allegations existed until he read the 75-page notice. Speaking with Fox News contributor Donna Rotunno, Metcalf said he was surprised by the scope of the filing.
Prosecutors also included photographs and videos they said showed Anthony with what appeared to be firearms, along with messages discussing shootings, robberies and narcotics.
The notice itself, however, is not evidence that those alleged acts occurred.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Instead, prosecutors identified them as evidence they said they might ask the court to admit at trial. The filing also cautions that some of the screenshots reflect only portions of larger text conversations.

Burks said prior alleged conduct can become especially important when a defendant argues self-defense because prosecutors often try to show the defendant – not the alleged victim – was actually the first aggressor. Rather than trying to prove someone has a violent character, prosecutors may argue prior conduct helps explain who started the confrontation, intent or another issue permitted under Rule 404(b).

"The prosecution can file a 404(b) notice to provide some information that can show that the defendant was, in fact, the first aggressor in the situation by showing information of previous aggressive acts," Burks said. "They can also use it to rebut a defensive theory."
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
Austin Metcalf was murdered under a track tent when convicted killer Karmelo Anthony stabbed him at a Frisco, Texas high school track meet. (Collin County Courts)

Anthony argued he acted in self-defense when he fatally stabbed Metcalf during an altercation at a Frisco track meet. Prosecutors filed the 404(b) notice roughly a month before trial, preserving the ability to ask the judge to admit dozens of alleged prior acts if they later became relevant during trial.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

The Collin County jury ultimately rejected Anthony's self-defense claim. Instead, the jury convicted him of murder and sentenced him to 35 years in prison after hearing testimony from more than 20 witnesses and reviewing surveillance video from the track meet.
SEND US A TIP
Whether jurors ultimately hear that evidence, Burks said, is a separate question.
GOT A TIP?
A judge must first decide whether each item is admissible under the rules of evidence before it can be presented in court.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Burks said many people mistakenly assume a lengthy Rule 404(b) filing means every allegation inside it will eventually be placed before a jury.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

"I think probably the biggest misconception people have about 404(b) is they think that because you've given the other side notice of it, that it's automatically going to come in," Burks said. "That is not what it means."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Whether jurors ever hear prior-act evidence depends on what prosecutors ultimately seek to introduce and what the judge decides to admit.
Fox News Digital reached out to Anthony's attorney and the prosecutors' office for comment.

story: The Fond du Lac County Sheriff’s Office released video showing a high-speed pursuit, cornfield search and arrest of a wanted 40-year-old man on Aug. 17, 2026.

Everyone in the Iowa Hill area is urged to lock their doors and remain inside. (Placer County Sheriff’s Office)

title: Patrick Clancy in his own words: Top takeaways from grieving father's first interview
summary: Patrick Clancy told "60 Minutes" that baby Callan died in his arms after four agonizing days and recalled apologizing to his son in their final moments.
story: Retired Massachusetts Superior Court Judge Jack Lu explains why the Supreme Judicial Court's ruling means a future jury could hear thousands of psychiatric records excluded from Latarsha Sanders' first murder trial.
Patrick Clancy begged for just one of his children to survive, held baby Callan as he died in his arms and revealed why he forgave Lindsay after she killed their three children.

Speaking with correspondent Ross Douthat on CBS News' "60 Minutes," the grieving father shared new details about his children's final moments, what Lindsay told him about the killings and the online attacks he says are hurting their legacy.

The interview aired after Lindsay's triple-murder trial ended in a mistrial. Her attorneys argued she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and was not criminally responsible, while prosecutors maintained she knew what she was doing.
From his desperate plea at the hospital to the online claims that followed the mistrial, Patrick described how the tragedy has shaped every part of his life.
PATRICK CLANCY SPEAKS OUT AFTER HUNG JURY IN LINDSAY CLANCY CASE, ADDRESSES PROSPECT OF ANOTHER TRIAL
Patrick Clancy on the stand at Lindsay Clancy's murder trial on July 29, 2026. (David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)
‘Just give me one’
Patrick said he clung to hope that Callan might survive after his siblings, 5-year-old Cora and 3-year-old Dawson, were found dead inside the family's Duxbury, Massachusetts, home.
Doctors had restored the baby's heartbeat, and Patrick told Douthat he began imagining the life he could still give his youngest child.
"I remember that night, I really thought there was a chance that Callan would live," Patrick said.

"And I remember just thinking, ‘Just give me one. Just give me one kid,’" he continued. "And I would raise him as best I could, and I would give him the best life I possibly could. And I'd tell him about his brother and sister."
Patrick said that hope faded when he reached Boston Children's Hospital and saw the look on a doctor's face.
Callan's heart continued beating for four days. Patrick became emotional as he recalled apologizing to his son and spending his final moments beside him.
Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)
"I said, ‘I'm so sorry,’" he told Douthat, his voice breaking. "And I got to hold him. I got to lay down next to him. And he died in my arms."

While Callan remained in the hospital, Patrick said he held his son's hand and used his free hand to write about all three children. He told Douthat he feared their memories might fade if he did not put them into words.
Lindsay never asked for forgiveness
The tributes Patrick wrote also included words of forgiveness for Lindsay. He said she has never asked him to forgive her, but he chose to give that forgiveness anyway.
LINDSAY CLANCY DESCRIBED A MALE VOICE ORDERING HER TO ‘KILL HER CHILDREN AND KILL HERSELF’: TESTIMONY

Lindsay Clancy looks on as jurors enter the courtroom during Clancy's murder trial at the Plymouth County Superior Court in Plymouth, Massachusetts, on Sept. 4, 2026. (Greg Derr / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)

"I saw headlines that said, you know, ‘killer mom’ and ‘baby murderer,’ ‘monster,’ and none of them were accurate," Patrick said during the interview. "I believe that it was her mental illness that caused that."
Patrick said he also feared anger would consume him if he could not forgive her.
"I felt that if I didn't get there, I would be eaten up inside," he said.
When Patrick asked Lindsay whether she remembered killing their children, he said she described the memory as dreamlike.
LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS

Defendant Lindsay Clancy wipes away tears as she listens to testimony during her murder trial in Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026. (Greg Derr/Pool The Patriot Ledger via AP)
"She said it was like a dream, and she remembered it much in the way you would remember a dream after waking up," he told Douthat.
Patrick said he did the best he could as Lindsay's condition worsened but must live with what happened.
"I think I did the best I could with what I had at the time, and I live with the outcome," he said. "I live with it every day."
Grief left him unsure he would survive
Patrick told Douthat his grief became so overwhelming that he questioned whether he would live to see another birthday.
"There was a time where I didn't think I would live to see my 35th birthday, and I was completely fine with it," he said.

Patrick later left Duxbury for New York City, where he could grieve without being recognized. Five weeks after the move, on what would have been Callan's first birthday, he went to St. Patrick's Cathedral, lit a candle and told his son, "I love you, buddy."
"And I walk out on Fifth Avenue and I start crying my eyes out, and nobody cared," Patrick recalled.
For Patrick, being able to cry without drawing attention was exactly what he needed.
"I thought, this is where I need to be," he said. "I can grieve."
His Manhattan apartment remains filled with reminders of the children, including a baby sloth Cora carried everywhere and a photograph of Callan wearing an oversized bow tie, "60 Minutes" showed.
Patrick said they also return to him in vivid dreams. In one, Cora walked into the kitchen of the family's former home and hugged him.
"I just looked at her and it was like I basically just said, ‘Where have you been?’" he recalled. "Those dreams are so real."
‘Trial by TikTok’ fueled painful attacks

The mistrial unleashed what Douthat described as a "trial by TikTok," with online sleuths and influencers spreading baseless theories portraying Patrick as uncaring, unfaithful and even responsible for the children's deaths.
"It's deeply harmful to the legacy of my children," Patrick said. "It is a huge distraction from what really matters here, which is perinatal mental health, and it's done real harm to real people."
LINDSAY CLANCY’S EX-HUSBAND DETAILS ‘BIG SPIRAL’ AS EXPERT SAYS ONE PART ‘SCARED ME’ IN MOM’S MURDER TRIAL

Lindsay Clancy listens to testimony from Dr. Gregory Saathoff during her murder trial in Plymouth Superior Court on Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr /Pool The Patriot Ledger via AP)
He said the repeated accusations have made it painful to be in public and warned that people may start believing false claims if they see them often enough.
"After seeing lie after lie after lie, they start to believe it," Patrick said. "And that's what we're left with."
Patrick said he sought answers from Postpartum Support International, psychiatrists and other experts. Those conversations helped him begin processing what happened.
A new marriage and keeping his children’s memory alive
Patrick's wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, joined him for the "60 Minutes" interview and recalled first learning about his children after noticing their photograph on his phone during a coffee outing.
"I just asked, ‘Who are those cuties?’" Danis told Douthat. "And Pat had said, ‘Those are my kids.’"

Patrick Clancy and Rachel Danis hold hands as they walk through East Midtown in New York City, NY, Wedensday, September 2, 2026. Clancy's ex-wife, Lindsay Clancy is currently on trial for the murder of their three children in 2023. (Elder Ordonez/InStar for Fox News Digital)
When she asked whether they lived in Massachusetts, Patrick told her they had died.
Patrick and Danis met through a New York running club in January 2024. Their relationship deepened as they continued running together, and they married in New York City this April.
The couple also discussed starting a family.
Asked what he would tell a future child about Cora, Dawson and Callan, Patrick said all of his children would remain part of the same family.
"You have different relationships with your kids, but they're all your kids," he said. "And I can't wait to tell them about their brothers and sister."

Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Sept. 4 after jurors split 11-1, with 11 favoring a finding that Lindsay was not criminally responsible and one holding out for a conviction. Prosecutors have not announced whether they will try her again.

title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror makes new promise as lawyer warns of public attacks
summary: Lindsay Clancy's mistrial juror Michael P. Desronvil plans a personal statement while her defense team pursues a double jeopardy dismissal motion.
story: A mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case prompts holdout juror Michael P. Desronvil to defend his position through a statement. Criminal defense attorney Mercedes Colwin breaks down the juror's reasoning and outlines potential next steps for prosecutors in Massachusetts, including a possible retrial or negotiated plea deal as the high-profile legal battle continues.

The lone juror who blocked a verdict in Lindsay Clancy’s triple-murder trial has promised to tell his story in his own words as his attorney warns that jurors must be allowed to follow the evidence without fear of retaliation.
Attorney Edward Paltzik said Michael P. Desronvil, whose refusal to join the other 11 jurors led to a mistrial, will issue a personal statement in the "near future."
"Michael will be making a personal statement in the near future, in his own words," Paltzik wrote in a Facebook post.
Paltzik thanked those who sent emails, texts and voice messages in support of Desronvil, while acknowledging that others may disagree with the position he took inside the jury room.
CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR TAPS FORMER TRUMP LAWYER TO FIGHT BACK AS HE’S ‘DRAGGED THROUGH THE MUD’: ATTORNEY
Michael P. Desronvil, the juror whose refusal to join the other 11 led to a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial. (Fugitive TV)

"This country was built on intelligent debate in the public square," Paltzik wrote. "That’s the same reason we support the good faith right of an individual juror to follow the evidence and the law to wherever they take him or her, free from fear of reprisal."
LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE INDEFINITELY IMPOUNDS JUROR NAMES, CITING SAFETY AND 'DIVISIVE' ATTENTION
Michael P. Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial, which ended in a mistrial. (Fugitive TV)

The attorney’s latest comments come as the deeply divisive case returns to the national spotlight. Patrick Clancy, the father of the three slain children and Lindsay Clancy’s ex-husband, gave his first television interview on CBS News’ "60 Minutes" Sunday night.

Patrick Clancy discussed his grief, memories of his children and baseless conspiracy theories that have spread online since the January 2023 killings. His wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, also appeared in the segment with correspondent Ross Douthat.
JUDGE JUDY WARNS OF 'DANGER' IF PROSECUTORS DON'T RETRY LINDSAY CLANCY AFTER MURDER TRIAL ENDS IN MISTRIAL

Lindsay Clancy, 36, was tried on three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of the couple’s children, 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. The children were found strangled inside the family’s Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023.

Clancy admitted killing the children, but her attorneys argued she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors argued that the former labor and delivery nurse understood what she was doing and carried out the killings deliberately.
LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE CALLS MISTRIAL, THEN GRANTS DEFENSE ONE HOUR STAY FOR APPEAL

Lindsay Clancy looks at jurors as Judge Sullivan asks them to start deliberations for a sixth day during her murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Pool Photo by Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)

Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Sept. 4 after seven days of deliberations. The jury was split 11-1, with 11 jurors prepared to find Clancy not criminally responsible and Desronvil holding out for a conviction.
Desronvil later said he had no doubt prosecutors proved their case.
LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR ADMITTED 'REASONABLE DOUBT' BUT STILL REFUSED INSANITY VERDICT, FOREPERSON SAYS

Judge William Sullivan indicates he was going to declare a mistrial before changing course and giving Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney one hour to appeal as the jury in the case has indicated they they are unable to reach a verdict on Friday, Sept. 4, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)

"Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses and what the prosecution presents, I thought it was enough proof that she knew exactly what she was doing and planned," Desronvil said in a statement first reported by NewsNation and confirmed to Fox News Digital by Paltzik.
Desronvil said he tried to raise different theories during deliberations but was repeatedly cut off by fellow jurors who treated his questions as uncertainty.
LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT PRAISED AS 'AMERICAN HERO' BY LAWYER WHO SAYS HE REPRESENTS HIM
The fallout from the mistrial quickly spilled beyond the courthouse, with Desronvil facing intense public scrutiny over his refusal to move off his position.

Paltzik, who previously represented President Donald Trump in lawsuits against The New York Times, CBS and ABC News, told Fox News Digital that he is focused on Desronvil’s "health, safety and well-being." He has called the juror an "American Hero" and "Champion of Justice."
LINDSAY CLANCY LAWYER SAYS HE PLANS NEW MOTION TO DISMISS AFTER JURORS SPEAK OUT ON MISTRIAL: REPORT
Former prosecutor and behavioral health law expert Mark Astor previously told Fox News Digital that Desronvil appeared to have hired counsel to defend his name after being "dragged through the mud."

"The whole idea of the jury is sort of this sacred arena where jurors get to decide a verdict in a case," Astor said. "And now we’re taking what is really a sacred arena, and we’re exposing it to the public."

Plymouth County prosecutors have not announced whether they will retry Clancy. Her defense team has raised the possibility of resolving the case without another trial and brought in veteran Boston attorney Martin Weinberg to pursue a motion seeking dismissal on double-jeopardy grounds.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Clancy is due back in Plymouth Superior Court for a status hearing Sept. 29, when the path forward could become clearer.
Fox News Digital's Adam Sabes contributed to this report.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Cops flush homecoming prank plans after seizing 650 toilet paper rolls in ‘Operation Clean Sweep’
summary: Plainfield police seized 650 rolls of toilet paper in "Operation Clean Sweep" after masked groups targeted homes near Plainfield North High School.
story: Former prosecutor Margaret McLean tells Fox News Digital why police departments are targeting teen takeover organizers before events even happen, warning that these social media-fueled gatherings can turn deadly in an instant.
After warning students not to let homecoming pranks cross the line, an Illinois police department found itself staring down one very unusual haul.
Plainfield police intercepted a massive toilet paper stash allegedly headed for neighborhood homes after reports of masked groups targeting the area near Plainfield North High School.
"And yes… 650 rolls. We counted," police said.

Police displayed the haul under an "Operation Clean Sweep" banner and jokingly gave it an estimated "street value" of $1,708.66 after two nights of escalating complaints from the surrounding community.
TRENDING 'SENIOR ASSASSIN' GAME DRAWS STARK WARNINGS FROM POLICE NATIONWIDE: 'DANGEROUS MISUNDERSTANDINGS'
"Homecoming is not a free pass to damage someone else's property or disrupt their quality of life," the department wrote on Facebook.
FLORIDA POLICE DEPARTMENT GOES VIRAL WITH GENIUS STRATEGY TO CONNECT WITH COMMUNITY

Officers received double-digit calls for service involving teens on both Monday and Tuesday during a two-hour period beginning shortly after 7 p.m. in the area surrounding the high school, according to police.

Residents reported that homes and vehicles had been targeted with toilet paper, eggs, ketchup, detergent pods and other items. Police said groups of 20 to 25 people wearing hoodies and ski masks would "pull up" in several vehicles at the same time and "cause chaos."
STUDENT CHARGED, WEAPON RECOVERED AFTER 3 TEENS TARGETED IN INCIDENT LINKED TO HIGH SCHOOL TRADITION: POLICE

Toilet paper covers part of a parked vehicle in a file photo. The image is not connected to the homecoming incidents reported in Plainfield, Illinois. (Matthias Balk/picture alliance via Getty Images)
The targets were not limited to friends or classmates. Some of the homes belonged to families with small children or residents with no children at all, police said.
"At this point, we are seeing property damage and significant cleanup, and residents are understandably frustrated," the department wrote.
COPS HALT PLANNED 'TEEN TAKEOVER' AS OFFICIALS BRACE FOR A SUMMER SURGE IN CHAOS AND ARRESTS: POLICE CHIEF
Rolls of toilet paper are tossed through the air in a file photo. The image does not show the Plainfield homecoming incidents. (Martin Philbey/Redferns)
The department also made clear that the homecoming calls were pulling police attention from more serious incidents.

Officers assisted firefighters at a structure fire, helped Illinois State Police, made a DUI arrest and responded to crashes, intoxicated people, violations of protection orders and a family experiencing a mental health crisis, according to the post.
"In short, we DO have better things to do," police wrote. "So PLEASE, be respectful of your community and let us!"
The department did not say where officers found the toilet paper, whether any arrests were made or whether charges had been filed in connection with the reported damage.
CITIES BRACE FOR HOLIDAY WEEKEND TEEN TAKEOVERS PUTTING BYSTANDERS AT DEADLY RISK, FORMER PROSECUTOR WARNS

The Plainfield Police Department Law Enforcement Center in Plainfield, Illinois. Police warned students that destructive homecoming pranks could result in criminal charges. (Plainfield IL Police Department)
Police had laid out a "zero-tolerance approach" ahead of homecoming week, warning that pranks involving trespassing, property damage or dangerous behavior could bring criminal charges.
"‘It was just a prank’ doesn’t erase the consequences," police warned in the earlier post.
THREE SCHOOL SAFETY STEPS EVERY PARENT SHOULD KNOW BEFORE CLASSES BEGIN
The department said it was not trying to stamp out school spirit and urged parents to speak with their children before the festivities began.

title: California animal rescue operator charged with felonies for alleged 'inhumane and unsanitary conditions'
summary: Video shows the squalid conditions where 300 animals were found at Christine De Anda's unlicensed Los Angeles County kennel, leading to 35 charges.
story: A California woman faces 35 counts and up to 24 1/2 years in prison after authorities uncovered 300 starving, neglected animals at the "Rock 'N' Pawz" facility in Los Angeles County. (KTTV; Los Angeles District Attorney's Office)

A California animal rescue operator is facing up to 24 1/2 years in state prison after being charged with 35 felonies and misdemeanors for alleged cruelty to animals, as she is accused of leaving roughly 300 animals living in severe squalor.

Christine De Anda, 57, operator of the "Rock ‘N’ Pawz" rescue, faces 12 felony counts of animal cruelty, two felony counts of grand theft of labor, and 21 misdemeanor charges ranging from failure to provide care to operating an unlicensed kennel, according to the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office.
Prosecutors requested that her bail be set at $914,500 ahead of her arraignment at the Antelope Valley Courthouse.
FLORIDA MAIL CARRIER ACCUSED OF SNATCHING PETS ON ROUTE, TRAPPING 100-PLUS CATS AND DOGS IN ‘HOARDING’ HOUSE

More than 300 animals at the Lake Hughes, California, Rock ‘N’ Pawz animal rescue are alleged to have been forced to live in inhumane and unsanitary conditions, including animals suffering from dehydration, severe injuries and starvation. (Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office)

"For someone who calls herself an animal rescuer, there’s a fundamental responsibility to protect and care for the animals entrusted to her," Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan J. Hochman said. "Instead, purported rescuer Christine De Anda allegedly left these animals to suffer or die from starvation, dehydration, untreated injuries and painful urine and fecal burns in filthy conditions."

"After repeated citations and warnings, Ms. De Anda continued taking in animals she could not care for, leaving hundreds to endure prolonged suffering," Hochman added. "These animal victims cannot speak for themselves and look to us to protect them. My office will hold their victimizer fully accountable for her inhumane actions."

The charges stem from a March 20, 2026, search warrant executed by Los Angeles County Animal Care and Control (DACC). Investigators removed more than 300 animals — primarily dogs, but also cats, a pig, a rabbit, a goose and two goats — in what DACC Director Marcia Mayeda called the "largest companion animal search warrant and rescue operation ever conducted" in the department’s history.
117 DEAD DOGS FOUND AT ANIMAL RESCUE, MANY WITH GUNSHOT WOUNDS AS INVESTIGATORS PROBE FOR ANSWERS

The operator of Rock ‘N’ Pawz animal rescue in Lake Hughes, California, is also accused of violating multiple county codes, including operating an animal kennel without required land-use approval, maintaining unsanitary conditions and having structures with unpermitted construction, plumbing, electrical and grading work. (Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office)

"More than 300 animals were removed from severely inhumane conditions," Mayeda said. "Animals were living in and saturated with their own excrement, had serious untreated illnesses and injuries, were emaciated, and were forced to live in small crates without adequate room to properly lie comfortably. Our teams have worked tirelessly to stabilize them, provide the medical care they needed, and help them recover."
At least one cat was found dead from starvation and dehydration at the start of the investigation, authorities said.
FLORIDA MAN ALLEGEDLY KILLS FAMILY'S KITTENS IN FRONT OF TEENAGE DAUGHTER AS FORM OF PUNISHMENT: OFFICIALS

A 57-year-old Lake Hughes, California, woman who operated animal rescue Rock ‘N’ Pawz was charged with 35 felonies and misdemeanors after allegedly keeping more than 300 animals in inhumane and unsanitary conditions, including animals suffering from dehydration, severe injuries and starvation. (Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office)

"Sadly, despite all efforts, we were unable to save every animal due to the extent of their illnesses and injuries," Mayeda added. "DACC is deeply grateful for the support of the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Los Angeles, Pasadena Humane and Kern County Animal Services for assisting us with this rescue and the Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office for its commitment to pursuing justice for these animals."
The L.A. County DA's Office shared a video on YouTube of the animals at the shelter, showing the conditions that led to the charges.

"These animal victims cannot speak for themselves and look to us to protect them," Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said. "My office will hold their victimizer fully accountable for her inhumane actions." (Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office)

Prosecutors say De Anda continued to take in an increasing number of animals despite years of citations and warnings regarding her inability to care for them. She is accused of violating multiple county codes, including operating an animal kennel without required land-use approval, maintaining unsanitary conditions and having structures with unpermitted construction, plumbing, electrical and grading work.

title: Police officer, woman shot near Notre Dame after football tailgates
summary: A single gunshot near Notre Dame's campus wounded a woman and a South Bend police officer during a post-tailgate fight, with the shooter still at large.
story: South Bend authorities detail the chaotic post-tailgate fight that led to one bullet striking a woman and hitting an officer, potentially with shrapnel. (WSBT)
A single gunshot during a post-tailgate fight near Notre Dame's South Bend, Indiana, campus struck a woman and a police officer Saturday night, authorities said.

The violence erupted around 7:30 p.m. ET just as crowds were leaving the university's tailgating areas and heading toward Eddy Street Commons. According to South Bend authorities, Notre Dame Police told them a male suspect was seen armed and reportedly pointing a gun at people, but when South Bend Police found a suspect matching their description, the person was unarmed.

"As approximately 20 South Bend Police Officers were working in Eddy Street Commons and responding to that call, a single gunshot was heard near Eddy Street and Angela Boulevard," South Bend Police said in a Facebook post.
The post said officers soon found a woman with a non-life-threatening leg wound, and a South Bend Police officer with an injury from either a ricochet or shrapnel.
POLICE MAKE ARREST AFTER GUNFIRE DURING CALIFORNIA HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME LEAVES 1 DEAD
Eddy Street Commons near the Notre Dame campus was shut down for a police shooting investigation Saturday night. (WSBT)
Both victims were transported to a local hospital and are expected to make full recoveries. Police said the officer was "doing fine," and that the woman was "okay."

Notre Dame officials said the suspected shooter fled west from the scene, NBC 5 Chicago reported. The suspect reportedly remains at large. and was described as a heavyset Black male with dreadlocks, wearing blue shorts, a black shirt with a red and blue design on the front, and missing one shoe, according to the local report.
Police are still looking for a shooter who hit a woman and a police officer with a single gunshot after officers were called to a fight at Eddy Street Commons in South Bend, Indiana. (WSBT)
MULTIPLE PEOPLE KILLED IN SHOOTING AT IDAHO IN-N-OUT RESTAURANT, SUSPECT DEAD

Following the incident, police swiftly evacuated nearby businesses and parking garages. The South Bend Police Department locked down the busy commercial district for an active investigation, urging the public to avoid the area while a heavy police presence secured the scene.
Fox News Digital reached out to the South Bend Police Department for comment, but a spokeswoman did not have anything to add other than referencing what the department posted on Facebook.
A violent Saturday night in South Bend, Indiana, erupted not far from the Notre Dame campus after a postgame tailgate crowd moved to the Eddy Street Commons. (WSBT)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Another shooting later in the night, roughly one mile away, left at least two dead and another critically injured. There was no indication from police that the incidents were related.

title: ICE-led Florida operation nets 500 — including illegal aliens accused of murder, child abuse, cartel ties
summary: U.S. ICE agents partnered with the Lee County Sheriff and Florida agencies in a weeklong sweep that netted 500 arrests in Southwest Florida.
story: ‘Border czar’ Tom Homan discusses reports that sanctuary cities are preparing to sue the Trump administration over new guidelines that could withhold federal funding from them on ‘The Ingraham Angle.’

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement partnered with more than five other federal, state and local agencies in a weeklong immigration-enforcement operation in Southwest Florida that yielded 500 arrests.

Caught in the sweep, according to a statement from ICE, were: a Haitian charged with murder; a Honduran accused of molesting children; a suspected Mexican cartel member; a Guatemalan who allegedly tried to use a Taser on an officer during his arrest; and others with accusations or convictions of crimes such as battery, DUI, hit-and-run, domestic violence, possession of illegal drugs, driving without a license, resisting arrest and returning multiple times to the United States after deportation.

From Aug. 24 through Aug. 27, ICE agents teamed up with officers from local, state and federal agencies, including the Florida Highway Patrol, the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, the Florida National Guard, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and U.S. Customs and Border Protection.
An ICE-led operation in Florida led to 500 arrests of illegal immigrants. (Getty Images; U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement)
GEORGIA ICE SWEEP NABS OVER 700 CRIMINAL ILLEGAL ALIENS, INCLUDING SEX OFFENDERS, CHILD ABUSERS
Suspected murderer captured
During the operation, the Lee County Sheriff’s Office arrested on a murder charge an illegal alien from Haiti who has been seeking asylum in the United States.
ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT’S ‘OVER-THE-TOP’ SEXUAL ASSAULT ON ELDERLY WOMAN SENDS SHERIFF INTO RAGE: ‘OUT OF CONTROL’
Whycliff Longin, 28, allegedly broke into a home in Lehigh Acres, Florida on Aug. 27.

Just before 3 a.m., deputies responded to a 911 call from a woman who had "escaped an attack in which she was strangled and fought to survive before barricading herself in a bedroom," according to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office.
Deputies said they found Longin fleeing from a neighboring residence and took him into custody.
Then they found a second woman "deceased inside a bedroom, suffering from obvious signs of blunt force trauma," the sheriff’s office said.
Whycliff Longin, 28, was in the United States seeking asylum when he was arrested for murder, sexual assault and burglary in Lehigh Acres, Florida, on Aug. 27, 2026. (Lee County Sheriff’s Office)
ICE LODGES DETAINER FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WITH LENGTHY RAP SHEET AFTER ALLEGED JEALOUSY-FUELED KILLING
The medical examiner ruled her death a homicide.
Longin has been charged with second-degree murder, attempted murder, sexual battery and burglary with battery. He is being held without bond in the Lee County Jail and has an ICE detainer.

"My prayers are with the family of the woman who tragically lost her life, and with the survivor who showed incredible strength in fighting to live," Lee County Sheriff Carmine Marceno said in a news conference.
Captured: Suspected Mexican cartel member, alleged Honduran child molester
FIRST ON FOX: ICE QUIETLY ARRESTS JAW DROPPING NUMBER OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS IN MASSIVE DC AREA OPERATION

Elsewhere during the operation, ICE agents and troopers with the Florida Highway Patrol worked together to arrest a Mexican cartel member and a Honduran accused of molesting two children, a statement from ICE said.
In another location, after a tussle, officers arrested Noe Lux Castro, 24, a "criminal illegal alien from Guatemala who illegally entered the United States," according to ICE.
ICE ARRESTS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS CONVICTED OF ATTEMPTED MURDER, RAPE AND CHILD SEX CRIMES IN TARGETED CRACKDOWN

During the incident, Castro took a trooper’s Taser and attempted to use it against the patrolman, according to ICE. Castro had illegally entered the United States at an unknown time and location without inspection, the agency said.
He was charged with obstructing a law enforcement officer, resisting an officer with violence and resisting an officer without violence.

Noe Lux Castro, a 28-year-old illegal immigrant, allegedly tried to use a Taser on an officer during his arrest in the Fort Meyers area of Florida in August 2026. (U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement)
ICE ARRESTS RECORD 238 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS IN ONE DAY DURING SOUTH TEXAS ENFORCEMENT OPERATION

The sting also brought into custody Olmen Noel Vargas-Mendoza, 40, "a criminal illegal alien from Honduras," ICE said. He allegedly "illegally reentered the United States without inspection three times and has a criminal history of domestic violence."

Officers also arrested Marlon Rolando Calderon-Castellon, 43, "a criminal illegal alien from Honduras," according to ICE. He "illegally reentered the United States without inspection and has a criminal history that includes battery and illegal drug possession."

Carlos Humberto Monzon-Cabrera, 53, is "a criminal illegal alien from Guatemala" who was arrested during the operation, according to ICE. He "has a criminal history that includes battery and multiple convictions for operating a motor vehicle without a valid license. He illegally entered the United States at an unknown time and location without inspection."

Hermenegildo Andres-Juan, 52, is a "criminal illegal alien from Guatemala" who was brought in during the surge, according to ICE. He "illegally reentered the United States after a previous deportation and has a criminal history that includes driving under the influence, resisting arrest, hit-and-run and public order crimes.
"He illegally entered the United States on Jan. 10, 2025."
"We will not sit idly by and allow Floridians to be victimized."

Also arrested was Armando Coc-Yat, 39, a "criminal illegal alien from Guatemala" who entered the United States illegally without inspection on Dec. 4, 2018, according to ICE. He "has a criminal history that includes arrests for driving under the influence and hit-and-run.
"An immigration judge issued him a final order of removal on Nov. 16, 2021."

Rigoberto Vargas-Resendiz, a 52-year-old "criminal illegal alien from Mexico," also was among those arrested, ICE said. He "illegally reentered the United States without inspection three times," including on Dec. 9, 2018. An immigration judge issued him a final order of removal on May 26, 2011.

Also arrested was Daren Ruiz-Mejia, 37, a "criminal illegal alien from Venezuela," according to ICE. He "illegally reentered the United States without inspection" on April 5, 2016, and "has a criminal history that includes driving under the influence of liquor."

Melchor Perez-Garcia, 31, "is a criminal illegal alien from Guatemala" who was arrested in the operation, according to ICE. He "illegally reentered the United States without inspection and has a criminal history that includes driving under the influence, resisting an officer and obstruction without violence."

Officers also caught Samuel Mateo-Francisco, 33, "a criminal illegal alien from Guatemala" who "illegally reentered the United States without inspection on three separate occasions," including on Oct. 31, 2023, according to ICE.
The ICE-led operation in Florida netted 500 arrests. (Michael Siluk/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

"The continued success of these weeklong operations is a testament to the power of unity and our shared commitment to community safety," said Matthew Elliston, of Enforcement and Removals Operations (ERO) for ICE.
