title: Florida plastic surgeon accused of killing attorney in his office defends himself in murder trial
summary: Tomasz Kosowski represents himself in a death penalty trial for the alleged murder of attorney Steven Cozzi, whose body was never recovered.
story: Tomasz Kosowski, the plastic surgeon accused of murdering Pinellas County attorney Steven Cozzi, represents himself in his trial. (FOX 13 Tampa)

An unusual trial is underway for a Florida plastic surgeon, accused of murdering an attorney he’d opposed in court and disposing of his body in a dumpster before prosecutors say it ended up at the landfill.

Clad in an orange jail jumpsuit, Dr. Tomasz Kosowski, 47, is representing himself in court as he faces a first-degree murder charge with the possibility of the death penalty. He’s waived his right to a jury – the judge presiding over the Pinellas County trial is set to decide the doctor’s fate.
Kosowski was arrested in March 2023 in connection with the disappearance of attorney Steven Cozzi. He has remained in jail and insists he is innocent.
The two men met through a legal dispute.
Tomasz Kosowski was accused of killing Steven Cozzi. (Pinellas County Sheriffs Office)
FLORIDA PLASTIC SURGEON MAY HAVE MURDERED MISSING LAWYER IN LAW FIRM BATHROOM: POLICE

Cozzi had worked on a civil lawsuit beginning in 2019 involving money allegedly owed to Kosowski for work he’d done tied to personal injury cases. Cozzi helped represent the corporate clients Kosowski was suing.

During years of litigation, Kosowski developed a hostile attitude toward Cozzi, according to court records. He blamed Cozzi for his problems in the case and demanded that the attorney be removed as defense counsel, records show.
"He made a bunch of completely unwarranted, inappropriate accusations about Steve throughout the litigation," said Jake Pillsbury, an attorney who worked with Cozzi on the case.
Cozzi had told others that, during a deposition, Kosowski approached him in a restroom and "called him a scumbag" and "that he [Kosowski] was going to win," Pillsbury said in court.
Those close to Cozzi began to worry about his safety.
Cozzi’s husband, Michael Montgomery, had suggested arranging for "some kind of on-site security," if Cozzi had to meet with Kosowski again.
Blood-spattered discovery
On March 21, 2023, Cozzi and Kosowski both were scheduled to attend a teleconference hearing at 10 a.m.
Before that, it was a normal Tuesday morning, Montgomery said. Cozzi brought him his morning coffee and they had a short conversation before he left for work. That was the last time he’d see him.
About 10 minutes before the meeting, Cozzi left his phone, keys, wallet, and other items on his desk and went to the office restroom.
He never showed up for the scheduled teleconference.
NEW CALIFORNIA LAW EXPANDS DNA TOOLS FOR MISSING PERSONS INVESTIGATIONS
Later, Cozzi’s boss entered the restroom and found spattered blood, court records show.
Security footage from the day Cozzi disappeared shows a subject arriving in a silver Toyota Tundra around 8:30 a.m. The prosecution alleges it was Kosowski.
A man wearing dark gloves entered the building where Cozzi worked carrying a box "large enough to conceal a human body," according to investigators.
Steven Cozzi vanished in Florida. Tomasz Kosowski was charged with his murder. (Largos Police Department)
At 10:22 a.m., the same man exited the building pulling a wagon covered with a reddish orange blanket.
The man could be seen struggling with the weight of the cart while pulling it to the truck, records show.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
That day, the Tundra was driven to Kosowski’s home in Tarpon Springs, Florida, videos pieced together from multiple surveillance cameras showed, according to court records.

On the way, the truck passed a Flock camera that captured an image of "a red bag or blanket in a cart that appeared to contain what resembles a human body located in the bed of the truck," according to arrest records.

Two days later, investigators arrived at Kosowski’s home with a search warrant and found the Tundra in the garage with blood in the truck bed, on the driver’s side headrest, on the driver’s side floorboard and on the garage floor.
Cozzi’s DNA was found in the Tundra and Kosowski’s garage floor, court records show.
SEND US A TIP

In the search of Kosowski’s vehicles, investigators found a ballistic vest with a "substantial amount" of blood on it. They also found one iPhone and a "burner phone"––the term for an inexpensive, prepaid device meant to be discarded.
Tomasz Kosowski represents himself during his murder trial. (FOX 13 Tampa)

Law enforcement officials also found a vest meant to be worn by a medical first responder, sheriff's office patches, a foldable bike, a gas can, $282,000 in cash, two passports and black, industrial-sized garbage bags.
Investigators also found a black duffel that the prosecution has called "a murder bag." Inside, there were lighters, a Taser, scissors, brass knuckles, a crowbar, ski masks and a Guy Fawkes mask.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
The bag also contained a syringe, a needle and a vial of succinylcholine, a paralytic drug. It was labeled in a way that connected it to Kosowski’s plastic-surgery office in Miami.
Surprising maneuvers caught on video
After Kosowski was arrested, police informed him they’d be searching his body to collect possible DNA and fingernail clippings, and would be taking photographs of him, the prosecution said.
After that, camera footage from inside the patrol car shows Kosowski struggling to bring his hands from behind his back, underneath his feet and up to his face.
He then began to "meticulously suck on each of his fingers," a member of the prosecution team told the judge.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
"He's using his tongue and getting up underneath it and slurping. He's using his teeth almost as a nail file, trying to destroy any trace of evidence that might bring him back to Steven Cozzi."
The prosecution argues that Kosowski began planning the killing long before he allegedly murdered Cozzi.
Authorities say Steven Cozzi was killed at this law office in Florida. (Google Maps)
More than a month before the attorney’s disappearance, Kosowski allegedly visited Cozzi’s home without his knowledge and photographed a car in the carport, according to the prosecution team.
Kosowski also visited Blanchard Law Firm where Cozzi worked. He drove around the building and took photos multiple times before Cozzi’s disappearance, the prosecution has alleged.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
In early March 2023, Kosowski began searching Cozzi and Montgomery online, seeking information about their wedding and records about previous and current addresses, prosecutors said.
An employee of the building that housed the Blanchard Law Firm told investigators that a week before Cozzi’s disappearance, she found a man in a mask hiding in the office utility closet.
Suspicious, she asked him why he was there, court records show. He told her it was because of a power outage and walked away.
She watched him leave in a grey Toyota Tundra, investigators said.
Fingerprints matching Kosowski’s were later found in that closet.
Investigators never found Cozzi’s body.
Attorney Steven Cozzi was killed in his Florida law office, authorities say. (St. Petersburg Bar Association)
Searching for Cozzi

On the day Cozzi disappeared, Kosowski’s cellphone was allegedly tracked traveling toward his second home in Miami. He pulled off on a dirt road in South Florida near the Everglades where there’s a dumpster, court records show.

Records of his cellphone’s location show he returned to the dumpster two days later, the prosecution alleges. The team argues that Kosowski returned to the garbage collection container to see if it had been emptied.
Law enforcement later investigated the dumpster and a K-9 trained in human detection alerted on it, indicating the presence of human remains. But a body was not found.
Investigators tracked down the garbage truck driver who collected that dumpster on his route. He remembers that day.
"It was a smell that he had never experienced," a member of the prosecution team told the court.
"He described that smell as vile. He had to crush the trash back in his garbage truck so many times, because the stench was so overwhelming––and this is someone who is a garbage truck driver."

The day he drove that load, the garbage truck driver stopped at a store to buy air freshener because he "could not stand the scent that was in his nose while he was driving around," the prosecution said.
That smell was "Steven's body decaying in the Florida heat for two days."

Video captured by a camera mounted on the garbage truck captured the load from the dumpster tumbling into the truck. That footage shows "a lot of black industrial-sized garbage bags, similar to the ones that Dr. Kozowski had in the trunk of his car," a prosecution team member told the judge.
Video shown in court shows bags falling into the truck that are "consistent with a human body," the prosecution team said.
Law enforcement officers visited the landfill where the garbage truck dumped that load, but it was more than a week after it was deposited.
By that time, more than 6,000 tons of compacted garbage had been piled atop the load.
GOT A TIP?
Still, in an attempt to recover the body of Cozzi, they sifted through the landfill for days, officers testified in court.
"His hearse was a dump truck, and his burial site… is at the Collier County Landfill," a prosecutor told the court.
The prosecution team has called dozens of witnesses to testify before Judge Joseph Bulone.
In July 2025, a written plea of not guilty was submitted by an attorney representing Kosowski at the time. In that plea, he requested a trial by jury.
More than a year later, on Aug. 31, Kosowski told the court he’d changed his mind and wanted a judge to decide his fate.
His trial began on Sept. 14.

For the first three days of the trial, Kosowski sat mostly quiet, blandly staring at witnesses, taking notes and giving short answers to questions from the judge. On the fourth day, he began cross-examining some of the prosecution’s witnesses who had presented evidence.
He has objected to evidence obtained from his body, from his Toyota Corolla and from his residence, according to court records. His motions to suppress the evidence were denied.

On Sept. 18, the fifth day of his trial, he asked the judge to strike a key witness’s testimony about DNA evidence. He argued that the witness, a DNA expert, didn’t provide enough of his own interpretation of the numbers.
Bulone denied the motion, but said Kosowski could challenge the DNA findings in closing arguments.
Fox News Digital was not able to reach Kosowski for comment.

title: Alleged killer mom Corie Walsh ruled too dangerous to return home — but psychiatrist warns risk can change
summary: Forensic psychiatrist explains why a "dangerousness" finding isn't permanent for Corie Walsh, the Illinois mother held without pretrial release.
story: Northwestern's Dr. Stephen Dinwiddie discusses psychosis, dangerousness and why severe mental illness is often misunderstood, particularly in the case of Illinois mom Corie Walsh.

An Illinois judge found Corie Walsh too dangerous to release after prosecutors alleged the Frankfort mother posed a threat to her husband and three surviving children after she was charged with murdering her 2-year-old son, Barrett.
But forensic psychiatrists say "dangerousness" is not a permanent label. Instead, it is a forward-looking assessment that can change as a person's mental condition improves through treatment.
Walsh, 40, remains held without pretrial release after a Will County judge denied her request to leave custody during a detention hearing earlier this month.
LINDSAY CLANCY FIXATION AND ALLEGED PLOT TO POISON HUSBAND EMERGE AS ACCUSED MOM CLAIMS PSYCHOSIS

The judge also ordered that Walsh immediately receive psychiatric medication after her attorneys said she had gone days without treatment despite a hospital recommendation that she receive around-the-clock psychiatric care.

Corie A. Walsh, 38, in a booking photo provided by law enforcement. Prosecutors are asking a judge to deny her pretrial release following the death of her 2-year-old son. (Will County Detention Facility)

Prosecutors argued Walsh should remain behind bars because, beyond the allegations surrounding Barrett's death, she allegedly threatened to kill her husband after her arrest. The judge agreed, finding Walsh posed too great a danger to release before trial.
LINDSAY CLANCY’S FUTURE COULD REST WITH ‘PROSECUTION DOCTORS’ AS CASE ECHOES INFAMOUS MAINE KILLINGS: EXPERT
The ruling raised a broader question that extends beyond Walsh's case: What does it actually mean when a judge determines someone is too dangerous to release?
Under Illinois law, judges deciding whether a defendant should remain jailed before trial evaluate the person's current risk to others rather than punish past conduct.

Dr. Stephen Dinwiddie, a professor of psychiatry at Northwestern University with four decades of forensic psychiatry experience, said psychiatrists approach dangerousness the same way – as a forward-looking assessment rather than a permanent label.
VIRGINIA MAN ACQUITTED BY INSANITY IN KILLING FLEES US DURING 48-HOUR MENTAL HOSPITAL PASS

"Obviously we're talking more about what we're afraid they're going to do tomorrow," he said. "Part of that prediction is based on what they did yesterday... what they did in the past... and what they have said they intend to do."
Corie Walsh, right, poses with her husband and children inside a church. Walsh faces three counts of first-degree murder in the death of her 2-year-old son, Barrett. (Facebook/Corie Walsh)
Unlike a criminal verdict, which looks backward at what allegedly happened, dangerousness is designed to evaluate the risk a person may pose going forward, Dinwiddie said.
"It's pretty squishy," he said. "Dangerous to whom? Imminently or long-term? Dangerous in a physical way or something else?"
In civil commitment proceedings, judges often decide whether someone should receive treatment over their objections because they present a short-term danger to themselves or others.
Dinwiddie said the rationale is simple: "If we don't act, something bad is going to happen within a matter of days, if not sooner."
Dinwiddie said treatment can dramatically change how psychiatrists evaluate a person's future risk.
Police tape surrounds the Frankfort, Illinois, home where officers found an unresponsive 2-year-old boy. (Fox 32 Chicago)
SCOTT WOLF'S WIFE SAYS ‘MY BRAIN TURNED ON ME’ AS SHE APOLOGIZES TO FAMILY FOR 'PROFOUND HARM' AFTER PSYCHOSIS

"If they've behaved in a violent fashion while ill in the past and now they're ill, obviously that's important information and obviously that's something to worry about," he said. "The intervention, obviously, is to try to get at that particular symptom of illness and get it under control."

That can have legal significance because Illinois judges may reconsider detention if circumstances materially change, although any decision to release a defendant before trial remains up to the court.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
That does not mean Walsh will be released before trial. It means a judge's dangerousness finding is not necessarily permanent.
"I think most of us believe that our interventions can prevent tragedies," Dinwiddie said.
PSYCHOSIS EVIDENCE CHANGES EVERYTHING IN CLANCY JUDGE'S OTHER KILLER MOM CASE: RETIRED JUDGE
He cautioned that psychosis alone does not make someone dangerous.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

"I think one misconception is they're just different. They're not like us," Dinwiddie said. "The tragic fact is they are like us and severe mental illness can affect family members. It can affect anybody."
Police tape surrounds the Frankfort, Illinois, home where a 2-year-old boy died. (FOX 32 Chicago)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
Another common misconception, he said, is that people experiencing psychosis cannot think logically.
SEND US A TIP
"Within that delusional system, people can act in a very organized, very logical, very purposeful way," he said.
GOT A TIP?
He described that concept as "rationality within irrationality," explaining that someone can carry out a series of organized actions while acting on profoundly delusional beliefs.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Dinwiddie also emphasized that psychosis is not a matter of choice.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
"The fact that somebody has evidence of a psychotic process ... that is not a matter of choice," he said. "Nobody would wish that upon themselves."

Walsh is charged with three counts of first-degree murder in Barrett's death. Prosecutors allege she believed the toddler was the devil and also threatened to kill her husband and the couple's three surviving children after her arrest.
Walsh has not entered a plea, and the case remains pending.

title: US military strikes alleged narco-trafficking vessel in Caribbean, killing 4 'narco-terrorists'
summary: Video shows a Caribbean vessel erupting into a fireball as SOUTHCOM says it killed four alleged narco-terrorists in a drug trafficking strike.
story: U.S. Southern Command video shows a Sept. 19 strike on a go-fast vessel that officials said was operating along a known drug-trafficking route, killing four alleged narco-traffickers (Credit: U.S. Southern Command).

The U.S. military on Saturday carried out a lethal strike on a vessel in the Caribbean that it said was involved in drug trafficking, killing four alleged "narco-terrorists," according to U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM).

"On September 19, under the direction of #SOUTHCOM, Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere executed a lethal, kinetic strike on a go-fast vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Caribbean," SOUTHCOM said in a statement.
"Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel's active involvement in narco-trafficking," the statement continued.
SOUTHCOM said four alleged "narco-terrorists" were killed during the operation.
NEWLY UNCLASSIFIED PENTAGON IMAGES SHOW SUSPECTED DRUG BOATS AS OFFICIAL ISSUES DEADLY WARNING
Video released by U.S. Southern Command shows a suspected narco-trafficking vessel erupting into a fireball during a U.S. military strike in the Caribbean. (U.S. Southern Command)
Saturday's strike comes amid a monthslong campaign launched by the Trump administration aimed at dismantling cartel-linked trafficking networks.
SOUTHCOM has conducted dozens of strikes in the Eastern Pacific and Caribbean targeting vessels it says are connected to "narco-terrorists."
On Sept. 9, the military said it carried out a strike on a vessel involved in narco-trafficking that resulted in three deaths.
US FORCES OBLITERATE SUSPECTED 'NARCO-TERRORIST' VESSEL IN LETHAL EASTERN PACIFIC STRIKE, KILLING 3
U.S. Southern Command said the go-fast vessel was operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Caribbean before the military carried out a lethal strike. (U.S. Southern Command)
Following Saturday's strike, the Trump administration's campaign targeting suspected cartel vessels has resulted in at least 231 deaths tied to at least 69 reported strikes over roughly one year.
Video of Saturday's operation released by SOUTHCOM shows a vessel moving through the water before erupting into a massive fireball.

In recent weeks, SOUTHCOM has also released several videos showing military personnel intercepting and boarding vessels allegedly involved in narco-trafficking before removing their crews and sinking the boats.

A suspected narco-trafficking vessel burns following a lethal U.S. military strike in the Caribbean on Sept. 19. (U.S. Southern Command)
Many of the operations recently highlighted by SOUTHCOM have targeted vessels allegedly tied to Los Choneros, which the military has described as a violent "narco-terrorist" organization.

title: New Jersey mom charged with obstruction after 'missing' son found hiding in her crawl space
summary: A New Jersey mother reportedly told East Brunswick police her missing teen wasn't home, but officers found the juvenile hiding in a crawl space in her basement.
story: Three New Jersey teenagers who vanished from a train station were found safe in Connecticut. Authorities used K-9s and drones in an extensive search, but the motive behind their actions remains unclear.
A New Jersey woman was charged with obstruction this week after her missing son was found hiding in a crawl space in her home, authorities confirmed.

After the 17-year-old boy’s father reported that his son wasn’t at his scheduled drop-off on Tuesday evening, his mother, Jennifer Buckley, reportedly told police the boy wasn’t at her house, and she couldn’t find him.
She also reportedly said the boy didn’t want to go to his father’s home and expressed concern he might be a danger to himself.

"The East Brunswick Police Department initiated an extensive effort to locate the juvenile," the department said. "Patrol officers and other department personnel devoted significant resources to the search, while detectives conducted a follow-up investigation in the days that followed."
The investigation, which included entering the teen’s information into the National Crime Information Center, uncovered a number of discrepancies in Buckley’s story.

When police finally did search her home, the boy was found hiding in a crawl space in the basement, and officers determined he had been there the whole time and she helped conceal him.
There is no evidence he was harmed in any way.
The boy was found hiding in a crawl space in his mom's basement.   (Victor J. Blue/Bloomberg via Getty Images/File)

Providing false or misleading information to law enforcement undermines those efforts and unnecessarily diverts officers and resources away from members of our community who may need immediate police assistance."

title: Philly serial killer probe could expose larger network behind apparent 'snuff' films, expert says

"There may very well also have been a participation in distributing so-called snuff films to underground networks of people that are into this stuff."

title: Missouri woman federally indicted over chilling death threats allegedly sent to Austin Metcalf's family
summary: Sharifa Nicole Henderson faces a federal indictment after allegedly sending death threats to Austin Metcalf's family after Karmelo Anthony's conviction.
story: Newly released surveillance video shows Karmelo Anthony fleeing from the scene of the crime immediately after the stabbing of Austin Metcalf April 2, 2026.
A Missouri woman was federally indicted in Texas after allegedly threatening the family of Austin Metcalf after Karmelo Anthony's conviction in the teenager's killing.

Sharifa Nicole Henderson, 34, was arrested in Kansas City Sept. 11, two days after a federal grand jury in the Eastern District of Texas indicted her on three counts of interstate threatening communications.
Anthony's trial concluded June 9, and prosecutors allege Henderson made three separate death threats against the Metcalf family in the days that followed.

On June 10, Henderson sent a message through Facebook Messenger to one of the Metcalf family members saying she would kill them and put them in a body bag before stating, "now this is a threat take me to court [expletive]," according to the indictment.

Jeff Metcalf with his son, Austin Metcalf, a junior at Memorial High School in Frisco, who was stabbed in the chest by then 17-year-old Karmelo Anthony, a student-athlete from Frisco Centennial High School. (Courtesy Jeff Metcalf)
KARMELO ANTHONY SUPPORTER REPORTEDLY FIRED AS OTHER BACKERS FACE BACKLASH OVER VERDICT REMARKS

Again on June 10, Henderson called the Collin County government, which prosecuted the case against Anthony, and said she would "demolish" the Metcalf family and "strangle" one of them, according to the indictment.
And on June 11, prosecutors say, Henderson sent another threatening message on Facebook Messenger to a family member.

"Don't worry I'll kill you next," she allegedly wrote, according to the indictment. "I will hunt you forever until I kill you...I will be there. You will always have to look over your [expletive] shoulder."
If convicted, Henderson faces up to five years in prison for each charge.
Austin Metcalf and Karmelo Anthony (Jeff Metcalf; Collin County Sheriff's Office)
AUSTIN METCALF'S FATHER ACCUSES MEDIA PUNDITS OF TRYING TO MONETIZE HIS SON'S DEATH 'FOR CLICKS'
Jeff Metcalf, Metcalf's father, recently told FOX 4 Dallas-Fort Worth that his family has received more than 100 threats since the end of the murder trial.

The case drew national attention and became racially charged, with supporters of Anthony criticizing the lack of Black jurors and calling for his acquittal, while supporters of the Metcalf family gathered outside the courthouse seeking justice.
Anthony, 19, was convicted more than a year after fatally stabbing Metcalf, 17, during a regional high school track meet at Kuykendall Stadium in Frisco, Texas, April 2, 2025.
Anthony, then a Centennial High School student, made his way over to the Memorial High School team's tent and sat under it, according to investigators.

Supporters of Austin Metcalf and Karmelo Anthony clash outside the Collin County Courthouse in McKinney, Texas, before a verdict is announced in Anthony's murder trial June 9, 2026. The jury found Anthony guilty of murdering 17-year-old Metcalf in a stabbing at a Frisco track meet last April. (Juan Figueroa/The Dallas Morning News)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Metcalf, a student at Memorial High, then allegedly told Anthony to leave. Prosecutors said Anthony provoked the confrontation that ended with Metcalf being fatally stabbed in the chest.
Surveillance footage later released showed Anthony running from the tent. In police reports obtained by Fox News Digital, Anthony was heard telling arresting officers, "I'm not alleged, I did it."
Authorities would later say they found no evidence suggesting the two knew each other prior to the incident.
A Collin County jury sentenced Anthony to 35 years in prison. Last month, a judge denied Anthony's motion for a new trial, though the family is readying another appeal.

title: Law professor's killer stalked him 'like a shark circling' before ex-mother-in-law's murder-for-hire ambush
summary: Donna Adelson and Charlie Adelson were both sentenced to life in prison for the murder-for-hire plot that killed Dan Markel over a custody dispute.
story: Internet searches from conman Brian Walshe and voicemails from his mother, Diana, take center stage in a new Fox Nation special on the Ana Walshe murder case.
After leaving the gym, Dan Markel drove home expecting an ordinary day. Instead, his killer was waiting for him.

As he arrived home, the prominent Florida State University law professor was talking on the phone with music teacher Stewart Schlazer about school options for his children. Then the conversation took a terrifying turn.
"Can you please hold on a second? There's an unfamiliar person in my driveway," Markel said.
SLAIN DAD'S DAUGHTER KNEW ‘BLACK SWAN’ EX-BALLERINA SHOT HIM AFTER ONE CALL: 'SHE KILLED HIM, DIDN'T SHE?'
Dan Markel, a prominent law professor in Florida, was shot July 18, 2014, and died the following day. (Florida State University)
Seconds later, Schlazer heard what he described as "a loud boom."

"There are really eerie parts of those final hours," producer Lily Fletcher told Fox News Digital. "You look at the CCTV footage, and it's a normal day. Dan dropped off the kids at school, he's gone to work out at the gym and then there's a Prius driving around the gym car park. It never stops. It's clearly waiting for him.

On Aug. 22, 2017, Stewart Schlazer, a music teacher, recounts his 2014 phone call with Dan Markel. Schlazer said he was on the phone with Markel when Markel saw someone he did not recognize walking up his driveway before hearing a loud sound. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

"It's always reminded me of a shark circling," Fletcher said. "There was something just so sinister and eerie during such a mundane part of his day, just going to the gym. That really stayed with me. That's a really chilling part, just watching that footage."
A photograph taken at the crime scene where Dan Markel, a Florida State law professor, was found shot in his car in 2014. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)
Markel was shot in the head while sitting in his car in the garage of his Tallahassee, Florida, home July 18, 2014. The 41-year-old died the following day.
The case is the subject of a new true-crime docuseries from ABC News Studios, "Welcome to the Family: The Murder of Dan Markel," now streaming on Hulu.
Phil Markel answers questions from the media after Donna Adelson was found guilty of the murder of Dan Markel Sept. 4, 2025. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

It features exclusive interviews, including with FBI Agent Pat Sanford and a recorded conversation with Rob Adelson, the oldest Adelson son, who testified against his mother, Donna Adelson, at her trial. It largely follows the prosecution's investigation and trial evidence, while also including testimony and recordings introduced during court proceedings.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

A photograph of Dan Markel's arm shows residue consistent with that left behind when a gun had gone off. Markel was shot and killed while sitting in his car in his driveway. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

Markel married Wendi Adelson in 2006 after the two met online. The docuseries depicts prosecutors' theory that Wendi's mother, Donna, was a dominating, controlling figure in their lives with strong opinions about her daughter's choices.

Wendi Adelson, Charlie Adelson's sister and Dan Markel's ex-wife, testifies in court Oct. 26, 2023, in Tallahassee, Fla., clarifying details about conversations with her mother and her divorce. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

Wendi later said the couple's marriage fell apart after they had two sons, Benjamin and Lincoln. Their contentious divorce in 2013 centered on the question of where the boys would grow up. Wendi fought to move them to South Florida to be near her family, while Markel pressed to keep them in Tallahassee, where the parents shared custody.
According to the docuseries, Donna was furious after the relocation request was denied.
Donna Adelson is escorted out of the courtroom in handcuffs after being found guilty of the murder of Dan Markel Sept. 4, 2025. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

Prosecutors said the custody dispute became the catalyst for a murder-for-hire plot that would take years to unravel. They argued at trial that Donna helped orchestrate Markel’s killing after he stood in the way of letting her daughter and two young grandsons make the move south.

They also revealed that her son, Charlie Adelson, arranged for Markel's killing through his then-girlfriend, Katherine Magbanua, who connected him to Sigfredo Garcia, the father of her children, and Garcia's friend, Luis Rivera.
Katherine Magbanua, who was convicted in the murder of Dan Markel and is serving a life sentence, testifies in the trial of Donna Adelson Aug. 26, 2025. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

Prosecutors said Garcia shot Markel while Rivera drove the getaway car. Over the next decade, investigators used cellphone records, surveillance video, financial records and secretly recorded conversations to build the case.
"Investigators suspected members of the family were involved but weren't able to prove it beyond a reasonable doubt for a really long time," Fletcher said.
Sigfredo Garcia, charged in the 2014 murder of Florida State law professor Dan Markel, looks directly at the camera as a photo is taken. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

"And I think what really surprised me about the investigation was how incredibly thorough and how many needles in how many haystacks they went through to find the evidence, whether it was tracking silver-colored Priuses across Florida or going through thousands of phone data to find any links to the family and near the crime scene."

A diagram displayed in Tallahassee, Fla., shows connections between Dan Markel, the Florida State law professor who was shot and killed in 2014; his ex-wife, Wendi Adelson; her parents and brother; Katherine Magbanua, who dated Adelson's brother; Sigfredo Garcia, who had a relationship with Magbanua; and Luis Rivera. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

At trial, prosecutors painted Donna as the calculated matriarch of an affluent South Florida family with the means and motive to orchestrate the killing of the ex-son-in-law she "hated." Defense attorneys, however, insisted the state didn't have sufficient evidence to link her to the murder plot.
Jeffrey Lacasse, ex-boyfriend of Wendi Adelson, testifies in the trial of Donna Adelson Aug. 26, 2025. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

In 2023, Charlie, a dentist, was convicted of first-degree murder, conspiracy to commit murder and solicitation to commit murder in his former brother-in-law's killing. Prosecutors told jurors that Charlie paid to have Markel killed and used Magbanua to hire Garcia. They said Garcia enlisted the help of Rivera, his childhood friend.

Charlie Adelson is cross-examined by Assistant State Attorney Georgia Cappleman during his trial for the murder of Dan Markel Nov. 3, 2023. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

Charlie testified that he had nothing to do with the killing and was stunned when Magbanua arrived at his home and said her friends were the killers. According to reports, he also said he needed to pay more than $300,000 in 48 hours or he would be killed. He was sentenced to life in prison.
Donna Adelson looks toward her husband, Harvey Adelson, Oct. 13, 2025, during her sentencing for her role in the murder of Dan Markel. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)
Magbanua and Garcia were convicted of first-degree murder, and Rivera was sentenced to 19 years in prison after pleading guilty to second-degree murder and cooperating with prosecutors.

Luis Rivera, one of the convicted hitmen who killed Dan Markel, testifies in Donna Adelson's trial Aug. 22, 2025. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

In 2025, Donna was convicted of first-degree murder, conspiracy to commit murder and solicitation to commit murder. She was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole and an additional 30 years for the conspiracy and solicitation convictions.

A photo of Sigfredo Garcia with his younger cousins is displayed during his sentencing for the 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel Oct. 14, 2019. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)
While Fletcher said the surveillance video is one of the documentary's most haunting moments, she believes the hundreds of FBI wiretap recordings provide the clearest window into the Adelson family.
GET REAL-TIME UPDATES DIRECTLY ON THE TRUE CRIME HUB
Large photographs of Donna Adelson and Dan Markel are displayed during the defense's opening statements in Donna Adelson's trial Aug. 22, 2025. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

"There are hundreds of wiretapped phone calls of the Adelson family," Fletcher said. "As a team, we listened to all of them. I think just the brazen way with which the family was continuing their lives during the investigation, really believing that they'd got away from it, was very disturbing. They really thought that they were above the law."
Dan Markel's home on Trescott Drive. Markel was shot and killed in 2014. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)
Fletcher said listening to the wiretaps left her with the impression that some family members believed they would avoid accountability.

"They weren't used to not getting their way," Fletcher continued. "And I think that is really alarming to me, that there are people like that who believe that they can operate outside of the constraints of the law."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Snippets of conversations Donna Adelson had with her daughter, Wendi Adelson, were displayed during opening statements Aug. 22, 2025. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

Two years after Markel's murder, Donna and Charlie spent hours discussing Wendi's boyfriend at the time and whether she should stay in the relationship. Fletcher said the conversations showed her how deeply Donna and Charlie involved themselves in Wendi's personal life.
Harvey Adelson hangs his head as a guilty verdict is read for his wife, Donna Adelson, Sept. 4, 2025. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

"It's hours and hours of conversations," Fletcher said. "It's Donna encouraging Charlie, and Charlie is suggesting to his mother as well that he will go and speak to Wendi. Just the meddling and the way they're speaking about Wendi and making decisions for her life, I felt that to be obviously really damning for them about their involvement in the case in terms of what the dynamics are like in their family."

Wendi Adelson watches as people leave the courtroom for lunch Aug. 25, 2025. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)
Wendi has repeatedly denied any involvement in her ex-husband's killing and has not been charged.

"I don't know why people online have such strong levels of certainty," Fletcher said. "In listening to the wiretap conversations of Wendi's mother and brother, and the way they are so accustomed to meddling in her life and deciding what is best for her, I could imagine a scenario in which she wasn't involved in it at all. I think that the vitriol around Wendi, especially online, is sad in a way. I imagine a scenario in which Wendi's family did this without her knowledge."

Phil Markel buries his face in his hands after hearing a jury find Charlie Adelson guilty on all three counts in the murder of his son, Dan Markel, in Tallahassee, Fla., Nov. 6, 2023. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

title: Clancy holdout juror taps former Trump lawyer to fight back as he’s ‘dragged through the mud’: attorney
summary: Michael P. Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy mistrial, has retained Edward Paltzik, a lawyer known for representing Trump.
story: Mark Astor, a former prosecutor and behavioral health law expert, tells Fox News Digital that the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy case retaining an attorney signals he needs to 'stand up for himself.'

The lone juror whose holdout forced a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case has retained a lawyer who once represented President Donald Trump, the attorney said. One legal scholar following the case said the move signals the juror is ready to "stand up for himself."

Clancy, 36, faced three counts of first-degree murder in the slayings of her children — 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan — who were discovered strangled at the family's home in January 2023.
Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Sept. 4 after jurors could not agree on a unanimous verdict, with the panel split 11-1.
Attorney Edward Paltzik told Fox News Digital Friday that he is representing the holdout juror, Michael P. Desronvil.
LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT PRAISED AS 'AMERICAN HERO' BY LAWYER WHO SAYS HE REPRESENTS HIM
Michael P. Desronvil, the juror whose refusal to join the other 11 led to a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial (Fugitive TV)

Desronvil, the lone dissenter from the jury, has come forward and said he didn't stray from his belief that prosecutors proved Clancy was criminally responsible in killing her three children in January 2023 in a statement first reported by NewsNation that was confirmed by Paltzik to Fox News Digital.

"I didn't have any doubts. As I tried to explain different possible theories during deliberation, I kept getting cut off as if I had doubts based on the evidence present," Desronvil said. "Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses and what the prosecution presents, I thought it was enough proof that she knew exactly what she was doing and planned."

Paltzik represented Trump in his lawsuit against The New York Times, which he said falsely cast his business success as fraudulent ahead of the 2024 presidential election. The lawsuit was dismissed in 2025 but has since been refiled.
Lindsay Clancy in Plymouth County Superior Court (Pool)

Paltzik was also involved in Trump's lawsuit against CBS after "60 Minutes" was accused of selectively editing an interview with then-Vice President Kamala Harris. In July 2025, Paramount Global agreed to pay $16 million, which the company said would go toward Trump's future presidential library.
Paltzik said at the time that the CBS interview generated confusion and "mental anguish" among viewers, misled voters and diminished attention to Trump and his online platform, Truth Social.
He also represented Trump during his lawsuit against ABC News, which settled for $15 million and the funds going toward his future presidential library.
LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR ‘LOOKED AT THE CASE AND HE MADE THE CALL,’ HIS BROTHER SAYS
Michael P. Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial, which ended in a mistrial (Fugitive TV)

In another high-profile case, Paltzik is representing three friends of Nolan Wells. Wells, 18, went missing July 4 after a boat trip with friends to Horn Island, a barrier island off Mississippi's Gulf Coast. Crews searched the area for two days before a National Parks Service ranger found his remains on the island's northwestern tip July 6.
Paltzik began representing the friends of Wells in August after several social media influencers made false allegations about them.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"We are proud to stand with and fight for three completely innocent young men: Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo, and Morgan Seymour. Starting today, those who wish to continue trafficking in lies about these Good Ocean Springs People will be held accountable to the maximum extent of the law. We, on the other hand, will be focused solely on the truth, which is that these innocent young men had nothing whatsoever to do with the tragic death of Nolan Wells," Paltzik said alongside Tyler Cox, a Mississippi-based attorney, in a statement to Fox News Digital.
Paltzik said Desronvil won't be doing any other media interviews at this time, calling him an "American Hero" and "Champion of Justice."
LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON SIGNALS HE'S OPEN TO A DEAL, HOPES DA WILL 'REVISIT' CASE
Callan, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Mass., home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)

"Again, we are focused entirely on his health, safety, and well-being. There will be a time for accountability and a time for the real story of the Lindsay Clancy Trial to be told. But not right now," Paltzik said on X. "This American Hero and Champion of Justice thanks all of you who have stood by him for your kindness, prayers, and support," he added.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
The statement was made as Plymouth County prosecutors weigh whether to retry Clancy, while her attorneys have also raised the prospect of resolving the case without a second jury trial.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE
Mark Astor, a former prosecutor and behavioral health law expert, told Fox News Digital it's clear Desronvil has retained counsel to "stand up for himself."
SEND US A TIP

"I think there's certainly some indication that his name and reputation is now being dragged through the mud," Astor said. "The other issue, obviously, is he's basically been attacked not just by potentially the other jurors, but by Mr. Reddington on the foot of the courthouse, since we had that mistrial declared by the judge. So, I mean, I think he feels like he needs to, you know, at least stand up for himself."
Astor said the exposure from the Clancy jury threatens a system that depends on people being willing to serve.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Lindsay Clancy in court last month (Boston Globe via Getty Images)

"I think it's a terrible thing that we're having to see this," Astor said. "The whole idea of the jury is sort of this sacred arena where jurors get to decide a verdict in a case. And now we're taking what is really a sacred arena, and we're exposing it to the public."

title: Hasan Piker calls Bin Laden a ‘spoiled brat,’ labels 9/11 ‘blowback’ in Axios interview
summary: Hasan Piker called Osama bin Laden a "spoiled brat" and labeled 9/11 blowback for U.S. foreign policy in the Middle East and Afghanistan.
story: Fox News congressional correspondent Bill Melugin reports on backlash facing Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed after far-left streamer Hasan Piker claimed that America is worse than al Qaeda on ‘America Reports.’

Hasan Piker, the internet streamer and YouTube personality known for his progressive commentary, called Osama bin Laden a "spoiled brat" for his reasoning in orchestrating the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks, which he called "blowback" for U.S. actions in the Middle East in the preceding years.

Speaking with Axios, Piker discussed bin Laden's remarks about why he targeted the United States: U.S. support of Israel, American oil policies and U.S. bases in the Middle East. He noted that bin Laden was once a U.S. ally when the U.S. trained, funded and armed the mujahideen in Afghanistan during the Soviet-Afghan War.

"The action was so heinous and so violent that — and also … given his position as formerly an American ally — I think that he came across a little bit more as a spoiled brat that wasn't getting his way. With many backers in the Saudi kingdom as well and the royal family," Piker said.
CLINTON, BUSH RECEIVED MULTIPLE WARNINGS ON BIN LADEN HIJACK PLOTS BEFORE 9/11, DECLASSIFIED FILES SHOW

Twitch streamer Hasan Piker is facing renewed scrutiny for his remarks during an Axios interview. He said Osama bin Laden was a "spoiled brat" and remarked on the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks. (Sam Barnes/Web Summit via Sportsfile via Getty Images)
The left-wing streamer said he wants fewer actors like bin Laden to "exist in general."

"The other path of least resistance is to not interfere in these affairs in general and not continue to dominate and create an environment where people are going to seek out revenge and put us in a position of danger," he said.
RADICAL EL-SAYED ALLY DOUBLES DOWN ON ANTI-AMERICAN RHETORIC WITH STUNNING TERRORIST COMPARISON
The World Trade Center in New York City after being attacked by hijacked planes Sept. 11, 2001. (Newspix via Getty Images)
Piker called the Sept. 11 attacks a "horrifying tragedy" and called them blowback for U.S. actions in the Middle East.

"Blowback is not a justification. Blowback is just what it is," he said. "A justification offers either a moral condemnation or a moral acceptance of the act. I do not accept the act of 9/11 morally".

title: ICE officer accused of lying to FBI about Minneapolis shooting pleads not guilty
summary: Christian Castro pleaded not guilty to six federal charges in the shooting of Julio Sosa-Celis during a Minneapolis immigration operation.
story: Fox News correspondent Christina Coleman reports from Dallas on a federal judge blocking attempts by Minnesota to extradite ICE agent Christian Castro from Texas. Castro faces charges stemming from the January shooting of a Venezuelan migrant during Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis, while Texas Gov. Greg Abbott investigates whether the officer legally qualifies as a fugitive.

A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer accused of lying to the FBI about a January shooting in Minneapolis pleaded not guilty Friday to six federal counts of making materially false statements.

Christian Castro appeared in a federal courtroom in St. Paul after prosecutors accused him of shooting 24-year-old Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis in the leg through the front door of a Minneapolis home during Operation Metro Surge.
Castro told investigators he was being attacked with a broom and shovel before opening fire, but prosecutors say surveillance footage contradicted his account.

During his court appearance Friday, Castro, 52, was wearing an ankle monitor and was instructed by a judge to travel only between Minnesota and South Texas. If he has any altercation with law enforcement, he is required to report it within 72 hours, the judge said. He was then released.
ICE OFFICER PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO LYING ABOUT MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING INVOLVING VENEZUELAN MAN

Christian Castro, right, an immigration officer accused of shooting a Venezuelan man during an immigration crackdown in Minneapolis earlier this year and lying to investigators, leaves with attorney Daniel Gerdts after a hearing at the Warren E. Burger Federal Building Friday in St. Paul, Minn. (AP Photo/Ellen Schmidt)

Castro was previously held in Texas custody for about 90 days before he was released. He was held for so long partly because Texas Gov. Greg Abbott refused to sign an extradition warrant to hand him over to Minnesota authorities.
Castro was booked in Minnesota last week following his release in Texas, his home state. Upon his release there, Castro was required to wear an ankle monitor and to surrender his passport and guns.
He faces federal and state charges related to the shooting.
ABBOTT TAUNTS FAR-LEFT AG WITH FIERY WARNING OVER ICE EXTRADITION FIGHT: 'SUCH BAD LAWYERS'
Christian Castro is charged with lying to investigators about a January 2026 shooting. (AP Photo/Ellen Schmidt)

Prosecutors said Castro lied about the circumstances of the shooting, which occurred during Operation Metro Surge, part of the Trump administration's crackdown on illegal immigration. He said he was being attacked with a broom and shovel before he fired his weapon.
The law enforcement operation saw thousands of federal agents in Minnesota that resulted in sweeping arrests, as well as the fatal shootings of two U.S. citizens.
‘UNPRECEDENTED’: JUDGES REVEAL BEHIND-THE-SCENES COORDINATION ON TRUMP IMMIGRATION CASES

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, left, and Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison, right, battled on X over whether an ICE agent involved in a recent shooting in Minneapolis should be extradited to Minnesota. (Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Minnesota authorities have battled the Trump administration over who should handle any charges against Castro. The administration contends that only federal authorities have jurisdiction over the case.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Michael Rapaport rips NYC Mayor Mamdani during Jewish gathering outside Gracie Mansion
summary: Celebrity Michael Rapaport slammed New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during remarks at a Jewish gathering on Friday, calling him "Zohran the moron"
story: Celebrity Michael Rapaport slammed New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani at a Jewish schools-related demonstration outside of Gracie Mansion on Friday.
Outspoken actor and comedian Michael Rapaport excoriated New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a Jewish gathering outside of Gracie Mansion on Friday.
"Zohran the moron is the most divisive mayor in the history of this city by far," the celebrity asserted. "He's a two-bit con man."
"His wife is an antisemite. His wife is a racist" as well as ‘a homophobic,’" Rapaport said.
MICHAEL RAPAPORT CHEERS MACKLEMORE GETTING DROPPED FROM ED SHEERAN'S TOUR, SAYS 'f--- YOU'
Michael Rapaport visits the SiriusXM Studios on March 31, 2026, in New York City. (Noam Galai/Getty Images)
The mayor's office on Friday responded to Fox News Digital's comment request by referring to remarks Mamdani made when asked earlier this week about the planned gathering.
"I welcome them," the mayor said. "They can have a vigil, or I've heard some describe it even as a protest."
Mamdani said whatever the gathering "is intended to be, they have the room and space to do so outside of Gracie Mansion."
"I think that at the time that they are there I will probably be somewhere else across the city," he said.

Rapaport said he is "absolutely considering running for mayor," though he left the door open to backing another candidate if that person would have "a better chance of winning." The next Big Apple mayoral contest is in 2029.
MAMDANI MAKES EYEBROW-RAISING CLAIM ABOUT NETANYAHU PROTESTS AHEAD OF NYC VISIT

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during a news conference to announce a lawsuit challenging the federal government's new public charge rule, which could make it harder for immigrants to obtain green cards if they rely on public benefits, at City Hall in New York City on Sept. 14, 2026. (ANGELA WEISS / AFP via Getty Images)
Rabbi Binyamin Krauss, principal of SAR Academy, a Modern Orthodox school in New York City, explained the plans for the gathering in a piece published by The Times of Israel.

"On Friday morning, students from SAR, Ramaz, and a number of other schools will stand on East 88th Street and daven. They’ll sing. A few of them will speak. Then they’ll get back on the buses and return to class, two days before Yom Kippur," Krauss wrote.

"Here’s what we want students to learn in the three periods this costs: you belong in this city, and when Jews feel unsafe we gather, and we pray, out loud. We express both our vulnerability and our agency at the same time. Showing up is a civic act, one the Constitution protects and one they’ll need for the rest of their lives," he noted. "Our students love this city and they love Israel, and they don’t see a contradiction."
