title: Pepper spray confrontation at AMC reignites frustration over phone use in theaters
summary: A man arrested after he allegedly pepper-sprayed a cellphone user at a movie theater has emerged as a controversial figure among moviegoers, with some branding him a “hero” and others condemning the act.
story: A man arrested after he allegedly pepper-sprayed a cellphone user at a movie theater has emerged as a controversial figure among moviegoers, with some branding him a “hero” and others condemning the act.
Police in Burbank, California, arrested 34-year-old Matthew Ware on Tuesday evening after he allegedly attacked another moviegoer for using their phone during a screening.

Ware was booked on suspicion of misdemeanor battery after allegedly spraying the AMC Burbank 16 patron when he became upset over their in-theater etiquette, Burbank Police Department Lt. Brent Fekety said. The spray affected two other moviegoers, who were treated for their irritation at a local hospital, according to Fekety.
Ware did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Sunday. It is unclear whether he has legal representation.
Online, the incident has become another flashpoint in the ongoing debate among die-hard moviegoers, for whom putting away a phone is a basic rule of theater etiquette.

Phone use in theaters has been a growing issue since pandemic restrictions were lifted. In recent years, as the box office rebounded into a Gen Z-driven boom, many moviegoers have lamented that the experience is now often tainted by fellow patrons’ full-volume conversations and persistent phone use.

In February, Alamo Drafthouse, an Austin, Texas-based chain that built its identity in part on a strict no-phones policy, began requiring patrons to use their smartphones to order food and drinks during screenings. The policy reversal drew swift backlash from moviegoers, who saw it as at odds with the chain’s long-standing ethos.
Last week’s pepper spray incident became social media fodder  after Joe Rodriguez, who witnessed the incident, shared a post to a Reddit forum for people in the AMC A-list Stubs loyalty program.

Rodriguez’s photos of Ware being handcuffed by police inside the theater recirculated on X and Instagram. His Reddit post about what he witnessed generated so much discussion that a moderator for the forum locked new comments in the thread, stating that users have “been down every rat-hole argument there [is] to have about this incident.”
“Not cool to pepper spray,” wrote one Redditor. “Not cool to be on your phone during a movie. Both things true.”

In a phone interview on Sunday, Rodriguez said the theater was less than an hour into a showing of “The Uprising” when he heard the hissing sound of a spray bottle going off. When he turned around, a man was covering his face with his hands while yelling that he got pepper-sprayed.
“Everyone was kind of like, ‘Was that real? What just happened?’” Rodriguez said. “So I got up and I was like, ‘You know what? I’m just gonna go get like a staff member, let an employee know.’”

Rodriguez, who was sitting in the row directly ahead of where the  alleged altercation took place, said he saw Ware immediately run out of the theater. He was followed by three moviegoers who appeared intent on chasing after him.
They soon found Ware lingering in the theater, and Rodriguez said he watched Ware defend himself to police during the arrest.

“The thing that stuck out the most was him saying that the guy on the phone ‘got smart’ with him, and that led me to believe that this wasn’t self-defense or anything,” Rodriguez said. “This was just a guy who was frustrated and lashed out because a guy was being rude at the movies.”

After the incident, Rodriguez said he spoke with the people who were exposed to secondhand spray in the theater. They said Ware had asked the patron he allegedly sprayed to turn off his device but that the person refused to do so.

Rodriguez said he didn’t expect the incident to drive so much discussion, particularly from those who defended the pepper-spraying. He said he believes many online are “living vicariously through” the incident.

“Because I’m sure in the moment, you want to lash out, and you’re like, ‘Oh, I want to teach this guy a lesson for being rude,’” Rodriguez said. “But ultimately what ended up happening is he kind of just ruined the movie for all those other people who got pepper spray on them, who had to go to the hospital, who had to do victim statements for people in the theater.”

As an avid moviegoer and AMC A-Lister, Rodriguez said he understands people’s growing frustration with the erosion of traditional movie theater etiquette, especially with the influx of younger moviegoers who sometimes struggle to put their phones away.

But people in Los Angeles, he said, seem to have a lower tolerance for poor manners in the theater. Perhaps, he said, it’s “kind of emblematic that this happened at the Burbank 16” — the most profitable theater in the country, frequented by entertainment industry types who take their moviegoing much more seriously.
Still, he said, the pepper-spraying was a bizarre reaction to witness.

“I deal with being behind the guy who’s on his phone, or behind the group of teenagers in the back of the theater who are constantly giggling and whispering to each other the whole movie, just being rude,” Rodriguez said. “You gotta choose your battles.”

title: Hunter charged with fatally shooting a woman he thought was a deer, police say
summary: A 74-year-old man has been charged in the fatal shooting of a woman after he said he mistook her for a deer while hunting, the Delaware State Police said.
story: A 74-year-old man has been charged in the fatal shooting of a woman after he said he mistook her for a deer while hunting, the Delaware State Police said.

Walter Moorhead of Salisbury, Maryland, was arrested after troopers responded at about at 7:40 p.m. on Friday to a report of a woman shot in an open field in the town of Ellendale. Troopers provided care before the 39-year-old woman was transported to a hospital, where she was pronounced dead.
State police identified the woman Sunday as Santos Maria Chilel Soto of Georgetown, Delaware.

Chilel Soto was walking in the field with a man and two children when Moorhead fired at her, according to state police. He was allegedly hunting from a camouflaged shelter, known as a “ground blind,” and believed he saw a deer and fired his rifle, striking Chilel Soto, according to police.
Moorhead was charged with manslaughter, reckless endangerment and possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony. He was released on $43,000 cash bond, state police said.
Moorhead did not return a phone call requesting comment on Sunday. It was not immediately clear whether he has retained an attorney.

title: Trump set to meet with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday
summary: President Donald Trump will meet with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani for a third time on Monday
story: President Donald Trump will meet with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday, the mayor’s office confirmed to NBC News.
In a statement, Mamdani’s office said the two would meet at Gracie Mansion, the mayor’s official residence, to discuss “issues affecting New York City and New Yorkers.”
The president will be in New York City for the United Nations General Assembly meeting, where he is set to deliver remarks on Tuesday and meet with global leaders.
This will be at least the third public meeting between Trump and Mamdani, who have previously met at the White House. The two first met in November 2025.
The Democratic mayor, who was first elected almost a year ago, and the president have had a mostly friendly relationship, though they have at times publicly criticized each other.

Prior to their first meeting, Trump described Mamdani as a “communist lunatic,” but after meeting with the then-mayor-elect in the Oval Office, the president told reporters that he’d be “cheering” for Mamdani and described him as a “very rational person.”
In an April interview with NBC News’ “Meet the Press,” Mamdani called his relationship with Trump “honest, direct and productive.”
He added that the pair get along as two natives of the nation’s largest city, saying, “New York City holds a very special place for him as well as for me. We’re both from the same city.”

Following their second White House meeting in February, Mamdani said he raised to the president the arrest of a Columbia University student by Department of Homeland Security agents. The student was released shortly after their meeting.
Despite Trump maintaining a chummier relationship with Mamdani than with other Democrats, the president has jabbed at him publicly.
Earlier this year, Mamdani rolled out his plan to impose a pied-à-terre tax on New York City homeowners who maintain a nonprimary residence in the city.

Trump derided the tax as “SO WRONG” in a post on Truth Social, writing, “Sadly, Mayor Mamdani is DESTROYING New York! It has no chance! The United States of America should not contribute to its failure. It will only get WORSE. The TAX, TAX, TAX Policies are SO WRONG.”
During his campaign last year, Mamdani called the president a “despot” and a “fascist,” remarks he defended even after his first meeting with Trump.
“That’s something I’ve said in the past and I say today,” he told “Meet the Press” after the Oval Office meeting.

“I think what I appreciated about the conversation that I had with the president was that we were not shy about the places of disagreement, about the politics that has brought us to this moment,” the mayor added. “And we also wanted to focus on what it could look like to deliver on a shared analysis of an affordability crisis for New Yorkers.”
Mamdani has also criticized Trump’s decision to go to war with Iran. In April, he blamed the military conflict for worsening a cost-of-living crisis in the city he leads.

“I wish that the words of Tupac from the ’90s weren’t still prescient, but they continue to be true for too many, which is that ‘We always have money for war and not to feed the poor,’” he told “Meet the Press.”

title: Presley Gerber Shared Mental Health, Addiction Struggles Before Death: ‘I’ve Had a Lot of Time to Look Into Myself’
summary: Presley Gerber shared his struggle with mental health and addiction before his death in a rehab facility at 27. What he said about drugs, alcohol, depression.
story: Presley Gerber was open about his struggles with mental health and substance use before his death at 27.
The son of model Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber passed away Sunday.
“The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time,” a statement on behalf of his family noted.
Gerber, who began modeling as a teen, once called dealing with mental health issues a “24/7 job” and posted candid videos he called “Mental Health Mondays” on his Instagram page.
How Did Presley Gerber Die? What We Know
Gerber died at a “rehab facility,” according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner.
No cause of death was given, but an exam of his body has been scheduled, the website entry notes.
He Spoke About Mental Health at an Event a Few Months Before His Death

In June, Gerber appeared with his parents at an event in Malibu, California, where he took part in a “candid panel discussion about mental health,” People magazine reported. It was his last public appearance.
“The most free I felt was when I was finally honest with myself,” he told the audience.
The model also offered advice about boosting mental health: “Move your body regardless of how you’re feeling. Get outside. Get some sun,” he said. “If you don’t feel like moving, lay on the grass.”

In December 2025, Presley spoke about his struggles in a since-deleted video on Instagram, revealing he’d largely given up drinking in recent years, noting that alcohol was “no longer serving” him, E! News reported.

He said he was taking various medications including Valium — the brand name for diazepam, which is used to relieve anxiety and control agitation caused by alcohol withdrawal — and buprenorphine, a medication to treat opioid use disorder, according to E! News.

He added he was also taking Xanax, the brand name for alprazolam, which is used to treat anxiety and panic disorders, for “when the panic attacks are really, really bad,” but was seeking more direction about his dosages.

“Every psychiatrist I’ve had — and I’ve had, like, 15 — they’re all like, ‘Here’s 20 medications,’” Gerber said. “‘Take this if you feel like this, take this as needed.’ And I’m like, ‘No, don’t give me that much leeway. I need some direction.’”
He Was a Mental Health Advocate
In a 2023 podcast, he said he struggled with mental health and depression, and wanted to help others dealing with similar issues.
“Whether I help one person or a 100 people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that’s all I need to do,” Gerber said.
“I’ve had a lot of time to look into myself and learn about myself with therapists.”
Mental health is “such a big part of my life,” he added, calling his focus on it a “24/7 job” and noting “there’s no judgement.”

“I’ve seen a lot of stuff and I’ve learned a lot of things, and what I hope I can do is have made the mistakes for some other people so they don’t have to make the same mistakes that I made,” he said.
He Tried Ibogaine
In a video he posted on Instagram in March, Gerber was seen in Cancun, Mexico, taking part in what he describes as a “Pre Ibogaine Flood Dose — quiet moment before everything changed.”

“I was absolutely terrified,” he writes in the caption. “Letting go of control didn’t come easy, but I trusted there was something bigger than me guiding it. I knew why i was there. I faced what I had been running from, and somewhere in all of it, i started finding my way back to myself.”

Ibogaine, a psychoactive compound found in the root of Tabernanthe iboga, a shrub native to Central Africa, has been studied for its potential in treating opioid and alcohol addiction, and other substance use disorders, according to the University of Virginia Division of Medical Toxicology.
It has hallucinogenic properties, and may prevent cravings and withdrawal.
Sister Kaia Gerber Spoke About His Addiction Struggles in a Recent Interview
After Gerber posted the candid video about his struggles in December, his younger sister, Kaia, praised his honesty and vulnerability.

“My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn’t share anything — and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, ‘I’m gonna be very human for everyone.’ There’s only so much you can hide from the world. And trying to put a lid on something just makes the person feel like you’re ashamed of them,” she told Vogue.
The outlet noted that he had a “decade-long struggle with drug addiction.”

title: What Dolly Parton Was Like ‘On a Personal Note,’  According to Kelly Clarkson
summary: Kelly Clarkson will always have a special place in her heart for Dolly Parton.
story: Kelly Clarkson will always have a special place in her heart for Dolly Parton.
Following the country legend’s death on Aug. 25, Clarkson opened up about her relationship with Parton while stopping by Studio 1A Sept. 21.
“She was just very cool as a human, not only as a musician,” she said.
Clarkson called Parton “such a lovely woman” and said she was “very sweet” and “very cool.”
“Even the first time I met her, (it) was like we’ve known each other for years,” she said.
Clarkson, who recently wrapped up her final season of “The Kelly Clarkson Show,” selected one of Parton’s most famous songs, “9 to 5,” to open the first episode of her talk show in 2019.
“That was our first cover. That was the first Kellyoke,” she recalled.
Clarkson described Parton as a “beautiful soul” and said she was a “pioneer for a lot of women.”
“She just paved the way for so many,” she said. “But on a personal note, she was so nice every time we ran into each other, like she was just so cool.”
In 2022, Clarkson had the opportunity to honor Parton during the ACM Awards and perform a rendition of the country crooner’s hit song, “I Will Always Love You.
While appearing on TODAY, Clarkson recalled how she felt when she was asked to pay tribute to Parton.

“I was like, ‘Of course! I’ll show up. Where do you want me?’ And then they were like, ‘Oh, she picked this song.’ And I was like, ‘What?’ I was like, ‘You want me to sing which one?’ And I was very nervous because that’s not a song anyone wants to touch. But yeah, but I would for her,” she said.
The same year, Parton and Clarkson teamed up for a duet of “9 to 5” for the documentary “Still Working 9 to 5.” At the time, Parton applauded Clarkson for her fresh take on the famous song.
“Nobody sings like Kelly Clarkson. She makes any song come alive,” Parton said in a press release, per People. “I love her voice on ‘9 to 5,’ and I am so proud I got to sing with her on it.”

title: ‘The Voice’ Welcomes 2 New Coaches for Milestone Season 30
summary: “The Voice” Season 30 has two new coaches sitting in the famous red chairs. Find out who is joining reigning champ Adam Levine and Kelly Clarkson.
story: “The Voice” will soon usher in the reign of a new queen for its milestone Season 30, and possibly an artist who is looking to take Blake Shelton’s king of country crown.

As the new season of “The Voice” kicks off, here are the official four coaches who are seated in the spinning red chairs when the singing competition series premieres. Joining returning coaches Adam Levine and Kelly Clarkson are two newcomers: country music singer Riley Green and icon Queen Latifah.
Levine was the first coach to be announced for Season 30 as “The Voice” officially announced “the champion” would be back in April. Then, Clarkson was confirmed on May 7.
“The Voice” waited a few days before surprising fans with the special announcement that two new faces were joining the NBC family.
Riley Green Takes a Seat in the Red Chair
On May 10, the show posted an Instagram video of Green, a four-time CMA and four-time ACM winner, listening to a voice message from Clarkson in which she welcomed him to the crew.

In the clip, she greeted him and said, “I’m super stoked to work alongside you. Welcome to ‘The Voice.’ I was stoked when I heard you were going to be a coach because I’m actually a super-fan of your music, man. You’re so good.”

She then added, “Needless to say, it is a competition so I, as a future friend, sent you something.” Clarkson explained that the gift was meant to help him prepare for his time as a coach before she “whooped that a--.”
“The Voice” later uploaded a video of Green sitting in his chair and practicing pressing his red button.
Queen Latifah Is Ready to Reign
The show saved Queen Latifah’s grand reveal for last, confirming her debut in a press release May 12.
Queen Latifah, already a Grammy, Emmy and Golden Globe winner with an Academy Award nomination, will soon try to add a “Voice” championship to her long list of accolades.

The multi-hyphenate and Green will look to dethrone Team Adam, who secured a victory in the Season 29 “Battle of Champions” finale in April with Alexia Jayy taking home the trophy. Levine and Clarkson are now tied with four wins each behind original coach Shelton, who won nine times.
Season 30 of “The Voice” premieres with a three-night premiere event starting Monday, Sept. 21 at 8 p.m.

title: Taylor Swift’s 3-Word Reaction to Travis Kelce’s 1st Touchdown of the Football Season
summary: Taylor Swift had an adorable show of support for her husband Travis Kelce after his first touchdown of the Chiefs 2026 season.
story: Taylor Swift’s show of support for Travis Kelce at the latest Kansas City Chiefs game left onlookers swooning.
The “Opalite” singer was spotted cheering on her husband at Arrowhead Stadium Sept. 20 during their game against the Indianapolis Colts.
Sporting a Chiefs tank top and jeans, the newlywed couldn’t contain her excitement as Kelce scored his first touchdown of the 2026 season.
As other fans in the stands began to cheer, Swift proudly pointed at her engagement ring and wedding band and said, “That’s my husband!” Then she proceeded to clap for the Chiefs tight end.
The NFL and Chiefs Instagram pages captured the moment and shared it, captioning the post, “@taylorswift is a proud wife after @killatrav’s TD ❤️.”
Fans of the couple, who tied the knot at Madison Square Garden in July, took to the comments section to share their love for Swift’s show of affection for her husband.
“Good job Travis, love how proud she is😍😍😍,” one commented.
“Love this couple! Pure joy,” another wrote.
One fan weighed in, writing, “I love this ❤️🙌🔥👏 Taylor is so excited for her husband and his team. I absolutely adore her. Never stop being you, Taylor. Your laughter and joy are infectious.”
Swift is jubilant in the stands, but has received criticism for the attention she’s given at games. The NFL regularly pans the camera to the singer during games.

In a 2023 interview with Time, Swift addressed the topic, saying, “I’m just there to support Travis,” she said. “I have no awareness of if I’m being shown too much and p------ off a few dads, Brads, and Chads.”
Referencing the quote, one Swiftie shared the following reaction to the latest video of the singer supporting Kelce: “It’s going to be a long football season for the ‘Dads, Brad’s and Chad’s hahaha.”
The 2026 football season only recently kicked off. On Sept. 14, Swift attended the Chiefs season opener and sat next to Tom Cruise.
While appearing on “The Tonight Show,” the actor later told Jimmy Fallon about the conversation he had with the singer.
“She was schooling me on football,” he said.
Cruise called the singer “a genius” and said he’s been “following her since she was a kid.”
“She’s funny. She’s got such a great sense of humor,” he said.

title: Gwyneth Paltrow Reveals Story Behind Her ‘Conscious Uncoupling’ With Chris Martin
summary: When Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin used the term “conscious uncoupling” to describe their separation in 2014, the phrase ended up going viral at the time, taking the internet by storm.
story: When Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin used the term “conscious uncoupling” to describe their separation in 2014, the phrase ended up going viral at the time, taking the internet by storm.
And now, we finally have its backstory.

Paltrow, 53, opened up about the term during a recent episode of podcast “Friends Keep Secrets.” It turns out, her introduction to the phrase came from a therapist that she and Martin had at the time.

“Chris and I had this therapist that was really brilliant, and he sort of introduced us to the concept,” Paltrow told hosts Benny Blanco, Lil Dicky and his wife Kristin Batalucco during the Sept. 8 episode. “We just made a commitment to really put the kids first, and so what that meant was to stay a family, even though we weren’t a couple.”
Paltrow — who is currently married to writer and director Brad Falchuk, 55 — shares two children with Martin, 49. The two announced the news of the divorce through a statement on her Goop website.

“We are parents first and foremost, to two incredibly wonderful children and we ask for their and our space and privacy to be respected at this difficult time,” Paltrow and Martin wrote in the statement. “We have always conducted our relationship privately, and we hope that as we consciously uncouple and coparent, we will be able to continue in the same manner.”
Paltrow told the podcast that when she and Martin decided to get divorced, she turned to friends who came from divorced households for guidance.

“I said, ‘Tell me, what was the worst thing? What do you feel you have scars from to this day?’” Paltrow recounted. “They said the worst part was ... ‘My dad used to drop me off at the end of the driveway.’ ‘It was so tense at my birthday parties.’ ‘They never ate dinner in the same room until my college graduation, and it caused me so much pain.’”

She added that she and Martin sought to “circumvent all of that awful stuff.” Paltrow also shared one particular trying moment during the divorce in which she had to put the conscious uncoupling philosophy to work. She explained that when the family moved to Los Angeles early on in the separation, they continued to have brunch together every Sunday. One particular brunch date proved difficult.

“Chris and I were upset with each other about something – I can’t even remember what it is — and I was like, ‘This might go really off the rails,’” she recalled. “It was getting tense, and we looked at each other. We went outside on the front porch, and we’re like, ‘Let’s just not.’”
She said that the two ended up embracing.
“We just hugged,” she said. “We like fist-bumped and then we went to brunch.”

Paltrow, to be clear, did not invent the term “conscious uncoupling.” The tactic, believed to be coined by late marriage and family therapist Katherine Woodward Thomas, has long existed with therapists and counselors encouraging the mindset as part of the final stage of marriage counseling after a decision to divorce is made.
Life coach Jeanne Byrd Romero previously told TODAY.com that conscious uncoupling is a method that can help the parties heal.
“It’s really a way of moving out of blame and shame so people can transform the experience into healing and peace,” Romero said. “It can be done with just one of the partners are the couple.”

title: Miley Cyrus Shares Her One Hilarious, Relatable Fear About Getting Married To Maxx Morando
summary: Singer Miley Cyrus recently shared the one reservation she has about getting married to fiancé Maxx Morando — and it is oh, so relatable.
story: Singer Miley Cyrus recently shared the one reservation she has about getting married to fiancé Maxx Morando — and it is oh, so relatable.
Cyrus, 33, spoke about the relationship in a Sept. 17 interview with Apple Music’s Zane Lowe. The singer, who got engaged to Morando last year, was brutally honest about her fears.

“We’ve been together six years, and I’ve never gotten the ick. But I was like, all of a sudden, got in my head,” Cyrus told Lowe. “I was like, ‘Oh my god, I’m about to get married. What if I get the ick?’”
The ick, of course, refers to that sudden onset of feeling of disgust when a love interest does something one finds awkward, embarrassing or gross.
Morando pretty successfully squashed the fear, Cyrus said.

“I asked him, ‘What happens if you get the ick once you’re married?’ He’s like, ‘You deal with it, and like you move on, and you don’t be a baby. The ick is for when you’re in fifth grade,’” she said.

Cyrus, who got engaged to Morando in Kyoto, Japan, has previously been married once to actor Liam Hemsworth. The pair separated in 2019 after eight months of marriage. The “Flowers” singer then met Morando on a blind date years later in 2021.
In the interview with Lowe, Cyrus said that her experience with the ick was put to the test shortly after she talked the subject with Morando.
“Then suddenly I got the ick,” Cyrus shared. “He did something that icked me for a minute, and I was like, ‘Don’t ever do that again. It gave me the ick.’”
It led her to wonder if she’s ever given her partner the ick as well, Cyrus told Lowe.
“He said, ‘When you’re a brat,’” Cyrus said of Morando’s ick. “Which is so true. Dude, I’m so icky when I’m a brat.”

Cyrus and Morando have been rather private about their relationship, sparingly attending events together. However both have spoken highly of one another. In a July interview with Wonderland Magazine, Morando said that he loves “going with her to certain things to support whatever she’s doing.”
Cyrus told Lowe in their chat that Morando has allowed her to “soften.”
“I realized so much of my life was performative that I didn’t even realize that he’s given me the permission to really like soften into the reality,” she said.

The pair have also collaborated professionally, with Morando co-writing multiple songs with Cyrus. Recently, the couple appeared together in the steamy music video for her aptly-titled song “Let’s Get Married,” shot at the Chateau Marmont in Los Angeles. The song is part of her new album “Bass Persuades,” which debuted on Sept. 18.

title: When Is ‘The Voice’ On? How to Watch the Season 30 Premiere
summary: “The Voice” is back for another season filled with inspiring singers, along with new and returning faces taking a seat on the famous red chairs.
story: “The Voice” is back for another season filled with inspiring singers, along with new and returning faces taking a seat on the famous red chairs.
Celebrating its milestone 30th season, the NBC singing competition show kicks off with a three-night premiere that starts on Monday, Sept. 21.

First up will be the Blind Auditions, the first round of the show, where singers will showcase their impressive vocals in hopes of getting the coaches to turn their chairs. Once a coach hits their button and shows interest in a contestant, they try to persuade the artist to be on their team.

Carson Daly returns as host, along with coach Adam Levine who won Season 29. Other coaches include Kelly Clarkson, who is back for her 11th season, in addition to newcomers Queen Latifah and Riley Green.
Find out the date, time and how to watch Season 30 of “The Voice” below.
What Day Does ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere?
The new season of “The Voice” premieres on Monday, Sept. 21 on NBC.
The Blind Auditions will continue on Tuesday, Sept. 22 and Wednesday, Sept 23.
What Time Does ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Air?
The first episode of “The Voice” Season 30 will air at 8 p.m. and end at 10 p.m.
The Sept. 22 and Sept. 23 episode will air from 8 p.m. to 9 p.m.
All episodes will be available to stream the next day on Peacock.
What to Know About ‘The Voice’ Season 30

“The Voice” is returning to its live shows format following the Blind Auditions and Cut Week, an elimination round. The six weeks of live shows will include special guest appearances and themed weeks. These episodes will be simulcast on Peacock.

During this season’s Blind Auditions, the show is introducing the all-new “First  In  Button.”  The button, which can only be used once, “gives the coach who turns first on a multi-chair turn the opportunity to claim an artist before the artist’s final decision,” the show’s press release said.

title: Alexis Ohanian Shares 1 Sweet Rule He And Serena Williams Have For Their Daughters
summary: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian shared how he and his wife, tennis icon Serena Williams approach their kids’ aspirations in life.
story: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian shared how he and his wife, tennis icon Serena Williams approach their kids’ aspirations in life.

Ohanian — who spoke to reporters Sept. 18 at the international debut of his all-women track and field league, Athlos, in London — told USA Sports that the couple just has one rule when it comes to the future careers of young daughters Olympia, 9, and Adira, 3.
“The one rule in the house is we don’t care what you want to do when you grow up, as long as you do your best at it and you’re doing something useful,” Ohanian, 43, told the outlet.

Ohanian attended the event with Williams, 44, along with their two children in a rare family appearance all together. The meet also included Olympic gold medalist sprinters Sha’Carri Richardson and Gabby Thomas, who are also two of the league’s athlete-owner advisors.
Ohanian explained to USA Sports that that day, Williams was tasked with monitoring their youngest, Adira. Meanwhile, Olympia was out, interviewing the star athletes.
Ohanian explained to the outlet that while Olympia was comfortable chatting it up with the athletes, she’s not firm on becoming a journalist.
“She hasn’t mentioned journalist yet,” Ohanian told the outlet. Right now, fashion designer is the number one career path that she’s circling around.”
He joked to the outlet’s journalist that their job is “safe for now, but watch out.”
“She’s coming for journalism,” he said. “She’s gonna go be great.”
Ohanian and Williams welcomed Olympia in September 2017 while Adira was born in August 2023. They’ve previously spoken about honoring their kids’ own passions.

In a January interview with TODAY hosts Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones, Williams shared that her children are in different sports that align with their personalities. Olympia, for example, is more interested in golf because she doesn’t like to run, Williams said, laughing. Adira may end up being the tennis player in the family, she added.

title: Celine Dion Dances Barefoot Atop Car After Paris Show In Ultimate Display Of Queen Behavior
summary: After a Sept. 18 show at the Plenitude Arena just outside Paris, France, power ballad icon Celine Dion surprised fans outside of her hotel with an impromptu performance in which she climbed up on the roof of a car barefoot and sang along with the giant crowd.
story: The queen is in her element.

After a Sept. 18 show at the Plenitude Arena just outside Paris, France, power ballad icon Celine Dion surprised fans outside of her hotel with an impromptu performance in which she climbed up on the roof of a car barefoot and sang along with the giant crowd.

Her iconic fan interaction comes amid her ongoing Paris residency that marks her first concerts in six years. Dion previously took a break from the stage after publicly revealing her stiff person syndrome diagnosis.
Multiple fan videos captured the magical moment. And it’s clear that the “My Heart Will Go On” singer is soaking it all up.

In the videos, Dion is seen climbing on top of the car and clapping along to her song “Pour que tu m’aimes encore.” Dressed in a more casual jacket and baggy pants, Dion engages with the enthusiastic crowd, dancing, playing air guitar and more.   She’s loving every second.

The past few weeks have been particularly significant for the artist, who has been performing in the City of Love amid a 26-date residency. During her first show back on Sept. 12, Dion made an emotional speech, reflecting on her return.
“I had promised myself not to cry,” said Dion, breaking down in tears. “But I’m so happy to see you all. I missed you.”
She added that she had always promised to come back to the stage — a commitment she kept.

“So here I am, singing for you,” Dion said during that first show at Plenitude Arena. “Thank you so very much for your support, your patience and if I may say so, I am everything I am because you loved me.”
Dion told the world about her diagnosis in 2022, canceling a string of performances at the time to navigate the condition.

Stiff person syndrome, a progressive, neurological disorder, causes stiff muscles in the torso, arms and legs, according to the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke. People with the syndrome can also experience greater sensitivity to noise, touch and emotional distress which can set off muscle spasms.
In the September cover story of Harper’s Bazaar, Dion revealed that she had experienced symptoms of the condition for 17 years prior to her diagnosis.

title: Ruby Rose Tears Up, Remembering Friend Hayden Panettiere: ‘We Spoke Every Day For 5 Years’
summary: Actor Ruby Rose recently got emotional while reflecting on the bond she shared with her good friend and confidante Hayden Panettiere, who died in August.
story: Actor Ruby Rose recently got emotional while reflecting on the bond she shared with her good friend and confidante Hayden Panettiere, who died in August.

Rose spoke about Panettiere’s passing during a Sept. 18 interview with Entertainment Tonight, sharing details about the friendship that the two shared over the years. The comments come weeks after Panettiere was found unresponsive at an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina. She was 36.

Rose — who was promoting the upcoming season of reality show “Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test,” on which she is a cast member — began to tear up while speaking about her connection with the late actor.
“That was my best friend,” Rose told the outlet. “We spoke every day for five years.”
Speaking to the outlet ahead of the show’s premiere on Sept. 24, Rose, 40, also revealed the way in which she met Panettiere.
“I didn’t even think we were going to be friends,” Rose said. “I didn’t know if I wanted to have any celebrity friends because I ... don’t have a great experience with the industry.”
Rose explained that while she was initially hesitant to befriend Panettiere, her reservations quickly dissolved.

“She saw me, and I just remember thinking, ‘Oh no!’ And then she ran up anyway and was like, ‘Hey, I’m Hayden. Can we go talk somewhere? We’ve got a lot in common,’” Rose said. “And then we went and talked, and we had everything in common.”
Rose told Entertainment Tonight that she and Panettiere would chat daily, texting and “checking in on each another.”
“It’s a bigger group now. There’s 14 of us that we’ve collected over the years,” Rose said. “That’s really — that’s my family.”
Rose added that all Panettiere “really ever wanted was to have her story told — her way on her terms.”
Panettiere was in cardiac arrest, meaning her heart had stopped beating, when emergency personnel arrived to the apartment on Aug. 16. Her cause of death has not yet been released.

Chief Deputy Coroner Shelton England of the Greenville County, South Carolina Coroner’s Office told NBC News Sept. 16 that the final toxicology results — that will determine Panettiere’s official cause and manner of death — are expected to be released within the next two weeks, he estimated, or possibly sooner.

Both Panettiere and Rose have been vocal about their negative experiences in the entertainment industry. Panettiere reflected on the trauma she endured first as a child actor and later on as an adult in Hollywood in her memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” published in May 2026.
“Reality merged with my imagination and burrowed into my core memories, where all my shame and trauma lived. Is it any wonder why I’ve faced so many real struggles in my life?” she wrote.

Rose has also voiced many of her difficult experiences. In 2021, she alleged that she was fired from the CW’s “Batwoman” after she was seriously injured on set. Warner Bros. Television Group denied the allegations, saying in a statement Rose was fired over multiple complaints about her behavior.
Since Panettiere’s death, Rose has posted on social media about the painful loss.
“Missing Hayden more than life today,” Rose wrote in a Sept. 14 Threads post.

title: Rescue Cat Named ChipPurr Jones ‘Throws’ 1st Pitch, Unites Baseball Fans Everywhere With His Cuteness
summary: What do Greg Maddux, John Smoltz and a teeny tiny orange rescue kitten have in common?
story: What do Greg Maddux, John Smoltz and a teeny tiny orange rescue kitten have in common?
Well they’re all iconic pitchers who’ve made their mark in the Atlanta Braves organization, of course.

The weeks-old kitten — appropriately named ChipPurr Jones after another Braves Hall-of-Famer — “threw out” the ceremonial first pitch Sept. 15 for the club’s Triple-A affiliate, the Gwinnett Stripers.
And the little guy delivered some heat ...by trotting alongside the ball to home plate.
To no one’s surprise, ChipPurr has since gone viral, with one post about the incredible outing amassing more than 109,000 likes as of the afternoon of Sept. 19.
ChipPurr’s handler Tricia Wurmstein, who’s also the Stripers’ manager of marketing tells TODAY.com that she’s proud of his performance on the mound.
“Honestly, it went so much better than I anticipated,” Wurmstein says, laughing. “He was ready for the moment.”
Videos of the miraculous moment show the kitten following a treat from the mound all the way to home plate as Ozzy Osbourne’s “Crazy Train” blares on the speakers.
Though there’s a ball in his periphery, he doesn’t interact with it at all. It’s really there for vibes.

ChipPurr’s pitching appearance was part of the team’s “Purr in the Park” night, which also included a pet supply donation drive, benefitting area rescue shelters. Fans were permitted to bring their beloved cats to the stadium for the occasion as well.
Like all pitchers, ChipPurr put in the work to make sure he delivered. Wurmstein helped him out with practice by incorporating treats into his “bullpen sessions.”

At first, she says, she positioned herself at home plate while he was on the mound in an attempt to see if he would run to her. But when she called out to ChipPurr, his trot was interrupted by the changing texture beneath him, she says. He wasn’t really feeling the pivot from dirt to grass.
“So I was like, ‘Maybe I can try and lead him with the treat, so he can directly see it and smell it right in front of him.’” Wurmstein recalls.
The rest is history.
Wurmstein says that ChipPurr came into the team’s orbit when he was spotted on a busy street a few weeks ago near the team’s home field in Lawrenceville, Georgia.

“One of our staff members happened to just be driving to work and saw him literally in the middle of the road in traffic,” Wurmstein explains. “So he got out of his car, scooped him up, and then brought him.”

ChipPurr was brought to a suite at the facility for safe keeping, Wurmstein says. And when word got around to her that there was a rescued kitten at work, the cat lover says she was swiftly on her way to meet him.
“I was like, ‘Yep, we will be keeping this cat,’” says Wurmstein, who’s been a longtime cat owner herself. “By ‘we,’ I mean me.”

As the person in charge of the team’s social media, Wurmstein says she not only began caring for the little guy, but she also introduced him to the team’s fans online. At one point, the team had an online naming poll for him, which ultimately led to his all-star moniker.
These days, ChipPurr, who’s estimated to be around six weeks old, lives at the stadium and has a whole apartment there with a ton of toys, including foam baseballs, Wurmstein says.
The proud cat mom adds that she’s got an eye on him at all hours of the day, even when she’s not physically at the field. She’s installed a camera to capture his movements, she says.
“I live literally three minutes from the stadium, so if anything were to happen, I’d be right here,” she says.
After ChipPurr starts his first round of vaccinations in a few days, he’ll join Wurmstein’s other cat for a cozy life at her home, she explains.

“I’ll start the integration process with them,” Wurmstein says of the cats. “And now that the season’s over on Sunday, it’ll be a lot easier for me to ... actually watch over them as they interact for the first time in the next couple of weeks.”
With all the attention from fans across baseball, Wurmstein hopes that his presence can help spread a simple message.

“Be kind to humans and animals alike. It’s great that we have Chipper now, but it was a really unfortunate circumstance in which we he came into our care,” Wurmstein says. “I just want to make sure that people are being kind to each other and being kind to animals.”
Now as for eight-time All-Star, two-time Silver Slugger and 1995 World Series champ Chipper Jones? He seems pretty impressed with his young protégé.

title: Watch How Amy Poehler Gets Famously Reserved Robert De Niro To Chit Chat More
summary: Leave it up to Amy Poehler to get a couple laughs out of one of the most iconically stoic actors of our day.
story: Leave it up to Amy Poehler to get a couple laughs out of one of the most iconically stoic actors of our day.

The “SNL” alum sat down with legendary actor Robert De Niro on the latest episode of her podcast “Good Hang,” released Sept. 15. While De Niro is famously known to be, well, not the chatterbox type, Poehler appears to get him to crack through a pretty nontraditional interview tactic.
“I’m gonna ask you a favor,” Poehler says, pleading with the actor. “If I don’t meet my word count by the end of this interview, I’m screwed.”
While De Niro seems to understand the assignment, he comes up a tad short when answering Poehler’s first question, “Would you consider yourself an introverted person?”
“In some ways I am,” he says. “Depending on the situation.”
And the comedian does not let him off the hook.
“We need at least 10,” Poehler replies, as the two dissolve into giggles. “We need at least 10 more words every sentence.”

During the podcast episode, Poehler and De Niro touch on a wide range of subjects from thirst traps to his new documentary “Tribeca 25,” which explores the beginnings of the famous film fest that he started with producer Jane Rosenthal after the 9/11 attacks.
The comedian truly hits it off with De Niro. At one point, she even moves him to tears when she praises his activism.
“It makes everybody feel very safe,” Poehler says of De Niro’s advocacy. “I’ve seen you do it over and over again, and I really appreciate it.”
Moments later, Poehler realizes that the comments have made De Niro emotional.
“This is going to be a real switcheroo,” Poehler says. “I can’t believe I just made you cry.”

title: Snooki Announces ‘Mawma Is Cancer Free’ After Diagnosis, Hysterectomy
summary: Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi announced in a Sept. 19 Instagram video that she is officially cancer-free.
story: Congratulations are in order!

Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi announced in a Sept. 19 Instagram video that she is officially cancer-free. The good news comes after the “Jersey Shore” star told fans in February that she was diagnosed with Stage 1 cervical cancer, undergoing a hysterectomy months later to treat the disease.
“After a colposcopy, conization & hysterectomy, mawma is cancer free,” Polizzi, 38, wrote in some text that accompanied a video of the reality star, enjoying a celebratory drink.
A colposcopy is a procedure that checks the cervix, vagina and vulva for signs of disease while conization refers to a different procedure in which abnormal tissue is removed from the cervix.
The announcement received an outpouring of support, including positive messages from fellow “Jersey Shore” cast mates Mike “The Situation” Sorrentino and Sammi “Sweetheart” Giancola.
Other social media users, who have also gone through cervical cancer, shared their excitement for Polizzi.

“I’m so happy for you and your family 🥹♥️ I know the struggle you have been through 🥹♥️I got diagnosed with cervix cancer in 2022 and went through chemo and radiation therapy, I’m cancer free now ♥️LOVE from Denmark ♥️” one user wrote.
In her post, Polizzi showed her appreciation for her medical team.
“Thanks to all the doctors who helped me on this journey!” Polizzi wrote in the caption. “It wouldn’t be possible without you!”
The reality star — who shared that she will be getting pap smears every three months to ensure that the disease doesn’t reappear — also encouraged women to be vigilant about their health.
“GET UR PAP SMEARS LADIES! & stay on top of those appointments!💗” Polizzi wrote.
Back in July, the mother of three shared a video on social media that gave fans a glimpse of her experience with hysterectomy surgery, documenting the entire day of the procedure.
“It’s a scary thing, and a lot of us women deal with it, and no one really talks about it,” Polizzi said in the video. “So I’m here to give that platform for all of us ladies.”

Polizzi also shared her honest emotions around the surgery. She said in the video that she was “terrified” while going into the procedure. The doctors ended up removing her uterus, cervix along with “some parts” of the vagina “just to make sure we get everything,” she said.
“Just dealing with all that pain — it’s not great,” a tearful Polizzi said.

title: Did Lizzie Borden Ever Have A Romance With Maid Bridget Sullivan? An Expert Unpacks the True Story Behind ‘Monster’ Season 4
summary: Did Lizzie Borden have an affair with her maid? What historian Cara Robertson said in an interview.
story: In Netflix’s “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story,” domestic servant Bridget Sullivan is portrayed as a seductive manipulator who plays a substantial role in the dynamics that lead to Lizzie Borden’s infamous trial for the gruesome Aug. 1982 murders of her father and stepmother.
But the sensational nature of the series has viewers wondering if the maid, played by actor Vicky Krieps, was truly the figure who was stirring the pot in the real-life Borden family all along.

It turns out, the true story of Bridget Sullivan was far less salacious. And though the season, which was released on Sept. 17, depicts her as entangled in a romance with Lizzie Borden herself, experts and historical accounts show that the pair had a professional relationship — one that never crossed into the realm of lust.

As Cara Robertson — author of the book “The Trial of Lizzie Borden,” which is largely considered the definitive account of the case — tells TODAY.com, it “sounds as if they want to make this a sexy story and it just isn’t.”
How is Bridget Sullivan Portrayed in ‘Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story?’
Bridget makes her mark not long into the first episode of the series.

After the Borden household goes through a slew of maids, Bridget interviews with the family and immediately impresses matriarch Abby Borden, Lizzie’s harsh, hard-to-please stepmother, with the way in which she is able to remove a stubborn blood stain from a prized fainting couch. Patriarch Andrew Borden is also struck by Bridget’s presence, drawn to her lack of queasiness around blood — something that’s important to him as a woodworker who builds coffins for a living.

But perhaps the person most captivated by Bridget is Lizzie herself, particularly after the new maid takes a special interest in her, introducing Lizzie to some more risqué things, including a hand-cranked vibrator. Bridget also attempts to ingratiate herself with Lizzie but emphasizing Abby’s poor treatment of her.
“I don’t know why she belittles you like that,” Bridget says to Lizzie in the first episode, entitled “Bloodbath.” “She’s the most cruel woman I’ve ever seen.”
Though Lizzie appears to be more sympathetic to her stepmother’s temper, Bridget’s tactic works. And before long, there are secret bedroom visits and intimate meetings between the two.

Their sexual tension-filled bond is cemented by the end of the premiere episode when the two share a bath of cherry juice, inspired by Elizabeth Báthory, a 16th century Hungarian countess who is said to have bathed in the blood of young women to preserve her beauty, though Bathory’s infamous blood baths are likely myth rather than truth.
Earlier in the episode, it is Bridget who gifts the story of Báthory to Lizzie.
What Was The Real-Life Bridget Sullivan Really Like?
The real-life Bridget Sullivan was indeed a maid for the family. But aside from that detail, the similarities between Sullivan and her “Monster” character are few and far between.

Sullivan, who hailed from Ireland, worked for the Borden family for a number of years, starting in 1889, according to the Lizzie Borden House. However, according to Robertson’s book, she was not always happy with her employment, telling an officer that she had attempted to leave the position on multiple occasions.

As the book points out, most of the members of the Borden family did not bother to learn Sullivan’s name, calling her “Maggie,” simply because that was the name of the family’s domestic servant before her.
Sullivan also wasn’t particularly entrenched in the family’s drama, Robertson says.
“Bridget was an observer of the family tensions.  She lived in the house and negotiated the dynamics,” the author says.
Nor is there any evidence that Bridget was a master manipulator, she adds.

The 25-year-old Sullivan did end up becoming a key witness in the trial, as she was in the home at the time of the murders. Though Sullivan testified over the course of two days, she was ruled out as a possible suspect.
So Did Bridget Ever Have A Romance With Lizzie?

Over the decades, many have attempted to romantically link Lizzie Borden with Sullivan, especially because the former was never married and considered a spinster for the time. But the truth is that there’s just never been any evidence that points toward a steamy affair between the two. It was all just strictly professional, Robertson explains.

“This is simply a newer version of a longstanding desire to give Lizzie a fictional romance,” Robertson says. “It’s as if writers and adapters of the story can’t make their stories work without inserting a love interest.”
What’s more, the real-life Sullivan had a rather sunny view of Abby Borden. Robertson says that Abby Borden was the only person in the household who bothered to call her by her real name.
“We really don’t know much about her relationship with Abby,” Robertson says. “Bridget spoke positively of her after her death, calling her ‘a lovely woman.’”

Bridget Sullivan herself did eventually marry. After the murders, she eventually found her way to Anaconda, Montana where she tied the knot with laborer and fellow Irish immigrant John Sullivan, according to the Lizzie Borden House. With the middle-class living that John Sullivan was able to provide, Bridget Sullivan left behind her work as a domestic servant. She refused, however, to speak of the murders ever again.

title: ‘Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story’ Reviews: Here’s What Critics Are Saying
summary: “The Lizzie Borden Story,” the latest installment in Ryan Murphy’s “Monster” series is raising a few eyebrows. Find out if critics think it’s worth the watch.
story: Ryan Murphy has just released “The Lizzie Borden Story,” the latest installment in his “Monster” franchise.

Like past seasons, which include “The Jeffrey Dahmer Story,” “The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story” and “The Ed Gein Story,” Murphy’s latest offering is a true-crime horror series. This time it focuses on a century-old murder.

Starring Ella Beatty, Vicky Krieps, Rebecca Hall and Charlie Hunnam, the 8-episode series is based on the real-life killings of Abby and Andrew Borden. Residents of the Massachusetts city of Fall River, the Bordens were violently bludgeoned to death in their home in 1892, with each receiving multiple blows with a hatchet.

Their 32-year-old daughter, Lizzie, was arrested and charged in the crime. However, after a months’ long trial, Lizzie Borden was acquitted of the killings. While it’s been 134 years since the murders, it still remains one of the most famous unsolved crimes in American history.

Murphy, in collaboration with Ian Brennan and director Matt Winkler, brings the controversial crime story to the small screen in his newest Netflix series. And much like his previous offerings, “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story” has been met with both praise and pans.
If you’re wondering if the crime thriller is worth the watch, see below for a roundup of the latest reviews and decide for yourself.
Aramide Tinubu, TV critic, writes in Variety that the new series “has a playful, vibrant tone” and offers “something refreshing and wholly unique to the ‘Monster’ canon.”

Tinubu also writes that Murphy’s take on the Lizzie Borden story is a “highly watchable depiction of one of the most gruesome crimes in American history,” while acknowledging that the storyline “bends and twists the truth” of what actually transpired in 1892.
The Variety critic also writes that parts of the series highlight “the obsession with women’s appearances across time” in a way that adds to the show’s “fun campiness and gothic nature.”
She concludes that “The Lizzie Borden Story” is a reminder “that the last person anyone should underestimate is a woman, especially one clamoring for even a small slice of freedom.”
The Guardian
Lucy Mangan, TV critic, is less flattering in her write up for The Guardian, calling the latest “Monster” installment an “utterly bonkers, blood-soaked, borderline-fetishistic fever dream.”
In her review, Mangan likens the creative process behind the series to “the gleeful disgust of a roomful of adolescent boys being taught about the female reproductive system in PSHE.”

While the real-life Borden murders are a deeply complex mystery, The Guardian review suggests that “The Lizzie Borden Story” offers a much simpler message: “Women be crazy! Especially women who menstruate!”
Mangan does acknowledge that the show is stylish with a “Wes Anderson feel at times” and that it’s “full of great performances.”

But ultimately, Mangan writes that “The Lizzie Borden Story” feels as though it was created by “a bunch of boys on a dare who should have been called back after class and made to get down to some real work.”
The Hollywood Reporter
According to The Hollywood Reporter, the Lizzie Borden drama is nothing short of “faux-feminist nonsense.”

Television critic Angie Han writes that Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan desperately try to draw “anything meaningful out of Borden’s saga” and do so “with all the finesse of a college freshman trying to crank out a 15-page term paper in the two hours before deadline.”
Of actors Hall and Hunnam, Han writes, “There’s zero nuance to their performances, and also nothing unique about them to make them memorable.”

With the murder mystery seemingly solved early on in the series, Han writes that “The Lizzie Borden Story” struggles with “having eight hours’ worth of content to fill” and that the show “flails about for a number of stalling tactics, none of them particularly satisfying.”
The Wrap
“Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan have never been particularly interested in letting a little historical fact get in the way of a good story,” notes movie and TV critic Matthew Creith.

In his review for The Wrap, Creith writes that the creative team behind “The Lizzie Borden Story” takes one of America’s most infamous murder cases and “gleefully blends it into gothic horror, sexual melodrama and blood-soaked camp” and that the series is “hardly a conventional retelling of the Lizzie Borden case.”
So much so, Creith writes “calling it ‘The Lizzie Borden Story’ feels almost deliberately misleading.”
The “poisoned meals, bloody corpses, severed heads” and “axes flying around” make the show “frequently hilarious, even when it isn’t necessarily trying to be,” observes Creith.
Beyond that, he also faults “The Lizzie Borden Story” for randoming including the addition of real-life serial killer Aileen Wuornos “for absolutely no reason.”
Creith does, however, laud Sarah Paulson’s performance as Wuornos, calling it “manic, twitchy and unnerving and that it captures Wuornos “without making the character another true-crime caricature.”
He also notes Rebecca Hall’s “shrill, vicious” portrayal of Abby Borden, calling it a “scene-stealer” in the series.

In sum, “The Lizzie Borden Story” is one where “patriarchal cruelty meets female revenge, with history merely the jumping-off point,” he writes before concluding, “If that sounds like a mess … it is.”
Rotten Tomatoes
Finally, if you head over to Rotten Tomatoes, you’ll find that the series currently has a 50% on its “Tomatometer,” which averages critics’ reviews into a single median score.
On the site’s “Popcornmeter,” which measures audience reviews, “The Lizzie Borden Story” currently sits at 26%.

title: Who Is Rachel Danis? About Patrick Clancy’s Wife, Who Is Speaking Out in a New Interview
summary: Patrick Clancy and his wife Rachel Danis are speaking out following the conclusion of his ex-wife Lindsay Clancy’s triple murder trial, which ended in a mistrial.
story: Patrick Clancy and his wife Rachel Danis are speaking out following the conclusion of his ex-wife Lindsay Clancy’s triple murder trial, which ended in a mistrial. The two married after Patrick Clancy divorced Lindsay Clancy following the 2023 killings.
So who is Rachel Danis, the woman who is now Patrick Clancy’s new wife?

Danis sat down alongside Patrick Clancy for his pre-taped appearance on CBS’ “60 Minutes,” which will air on Sept. 20. The interview marks his first since a judge earlier this month declared a mistrial when a jury — who had been tasked with determining whether Lindsay Clancy was criminally responsible for killing her three children — failed to reach a unanimous verdict.

During the trial, which ended Sept. 4, the prosecution argued that the mom had intentionally and knowingly attacked her children. Meanwhile, Lindsay Clancy’s defense did not dispute the fact that she had killed her children. But they argued that she is not criminally responsible for the murders, as she was consumed by the rare mental health condition postpartum psychosis.
Here’s what to know about Danis and her relationship with Patrick Clancy.
Who Is Rachel Danis?

Danis is a New York-based fertility doctor. According to her professional page, she’s specifically a reproductive endocrinologist and infertility specialist at clinic RMA of New York. She’s also an assistant clinical professor at Mount Sinai’s Icahn School of Medicine.

Danis specializes in endometriosis, an often painful condition in which tissue similar to what typically lines the uterus ends up on other organs. She also specializes in ovulation induction, LGBTQIA family building and fertility preservation, according to her professional biography. At one point, she was awarded a grant to conduct a clinical trial using Orlissa, a drug that aims to help patients manage moderate to severe endometriosis pain.

According to her professional bio, she’s somewhat of a fitness aficionado outside of work, and can often be found in a bootcamp class or ballet class. She also enjoys baking and strolls through Central Park, according to the website.
How Did She Meet Patrick Clancy?
Danis, who married Patrick Clancy in April, shared in a newly released clip from the upcoming “60 Minutes” interview that she met Clancy in Manhattan’s Central Park.
“I was just a girl that met a guy running in Central Park on a really cold Saturday,” Danis said. “And I don’t think there’s anything wrong with that.”

Patrick Clancy, who divorced Lindsay Clancy following the 2023 killings, relocated to New York from the suburbs of Boston after the tragedy. By Oct. 2024, Clancy was living in what the New Yorker described in a feature as an apartment in Manhattan that resembled a “tidy bachelor pad,” which included a few keepsakes from his late children Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months. Clancy did not comment on his relationship status with Lindsay Clancy at the time, nor did he mention Danis.
Lindsay Clancy’s defense attorney Kevin Reddington confirmed in court that Patrick Clancy had remarried and is “trying to move on.”
How Was Danis Impacted During The Trial?

While Danis did not take the stand during the nearly six-week trial over the summer, Patrick Clancy spent two days testifying on the events that led up to the killings in addition to Lindsay Clancy’s deteriorating mental health prior to the tragedy.

However Danis became a topic of conversation when conspiracies began to arise on social media from internet users who accused Patrick Clancy of killing his children. Others online have also accused the father of framing the defendant. And in the days that followed the trial, Danis and Patrick Clancy were frequently the subject of paparazzi photos in addition to harassment.
In the upcoming interview, Danis defends their marriage.

“I don’t understand how the story has been so twisted, but I would hope people know that Pat is, as I said before, the most selfless father and supportive partner,” she said in the newly released clip.

Patrick Clancy and others involved in the case have made multiple attempts to shut down internet conspiracies. In a Sept. 9 interview with NBC News’ Laura Jarrett, Reddington called on people to stop spreading misinformation and attacking Patrick Clancy.
“His life has been turned upside down into a nightmare that he doesn’t deserve,” Reddington said. “Period. Full stop.”
The defense attorney added that he has “said it repeatedly, unequivocally, that there is absolutely no way that this guy deserves what he has been living (through).”

The day prior, Patrick Clancy’s attorneys also attempted to shut down the noise from conspiracy theorists. One of his attorneys, Howard Cooper, mentioned in a statement that law enforcement “has been notified” about the claims and that “every appropriate measure will be pursued to hold them accountable, including legally.”
“This campaign, now fueled by insatiable media coverage, remains at a fever pitch and has resulted in real life threats to his reputation, livelihood, and life,” Cooper said in the Sept. 8 statement.

title: Lucy Foley Revives Agatha Christie’s Miss Marple For the Character’s First Novel in 50 Years. Read the Prologue
summary: Sleuth Miss Marple, created by Agatha Christie, has once again found herself at the scene of a crime in Lucy Foley’s “Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel.” Read the prologue.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
After 50 years away, cunning and perceptive sleuth Miss Marple has once again found herself at the scene of a crime.

The elderly character at the center of many Agatha Christie whodunits is tasked with solving a new case in Lucy Foley’s latest mystery “Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel,” out Sept. 22. Christie is also listed as an author.

Set at a secluded resort in Switzerland, the Grand Alpine is practically cut off from the outside world, only accessible via a gondola ride during particular hours of the day. And it’s precisely there that the book begins. The prologue opens with the line:
The gondola rises silently through the bank of clouds into the frozen world at the top of the mountain.

Foley tells TODAY.com the eerie, chilling setting was the perfect place to make Miss Marple — who last appeared in a novel in Christie’s 1976 work “Sleeping Murder” — the “beating heart” of the story.

The bestselling British author behind “The Guest List” and “The Paris Apartment” grew up a fan of Christie, discovering one of her detective novels on a bookshelf in a cottage when she was just 12. She devoured more stories but she didn’t appreciate Miss Marple’s character, she recalls.
It wasn’t until she re-read some of Christie’s novels that she admired how the writer took an “underdog character” and made “her a master sleuth with a brain to rival Sherlock Holmes.”

“It was so clever, and it still feels radical even today,” Foley says. “I think we still have an issue with older women being perceived as invisible or less capable in some way. I still think she has something to teach us.”

In 2022, Foley was asked to contribute to a collection of 12 new Marple stories, alongside Leigh Bardugo, Ruth Ware, Jean Kwok and more. When she was approached again about the character, this time for a full-length novel, she jumped at the opportunity.

“In 2026, we need a new kind of superhero. We’re surrounded by these male egos and these men rewriting history to further their own ends. I love thinking, ‘What would Miss Marple make of them, and how would she thwart them?’” she says.

Still, she initially felt the pressure of doing the character justice. But once she had her premise — Miss Marple on a holiday to the Swiss Alps in the 1950s — she entered her creative bubble and started plotting the mystery.

“It felt like quite a haunted time in many ways because there was this long shadow of the Second World War. I wanted that to be something that I contrasted with the glamour,” she says of the setting of “Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel.”

She also knew how she wanted to structure the novel. Fans of Foley’s other books will know that the writer tells each chapter from a different character’s first person point of view. With Miss Marple, though, she decided readers wouldn’t hear the inner workings of the detective’s mind.

“I knew that I couldn’t have her perspective because that would feel like a real Christie anachronism,” she says, laughing. “Because I think the really interesting thing about Miss Marple is she’s quite enigmatic, and she doesn’t actually necessarily reveal a lot of herself.”

The character works best as an underestimated observer, Foley shares, and she wanted to keep her that way. She read, and re-read, Christie’s books to nail Miss Marple’s tone and mannerisms. She also watched the British television series.

“There were two things that I knew I had to get right for this book before I brought in any of my own sort of creative sensibilities, and those were the Christie plotting… (and) also Miss Marple. So I wanted to get her on the page as closely as I possibly could to Christie’s Miss Marple,” Foley says.
Beyond that, she says she had “some license” to bring in her own voice and style.
“I wanted it to be a book that was in conversation with the original Miss Marple,” Foley says. “They didn’t want to present it as a kind of Agatha Christie forgery.”
With those goals in mind, Foley plotted out the entire book before she started writing, a change to her usual process.

While Miss Marple isn’t mentioned in the prologue, she is quickly introduced in Chapter 1, which is told from the perspective of Diana Glass, described as “the help.” Diana meets Miss Marple and describes her as a “the perfect image of a little old lady — almost too perfect, in fact.”

“I wanted, through Diana’s eyes, a reader who’s familiar with Miss Marple to recognize this character that they know and love. But also a reader coming to her completely cold, not knowing much about her, to quite quickly get a sense of who she is through Diana’s perspective,” Foley says.
Readers then meet more characters who will all become suspects in the death of the unnamed person found in the gondola. Miss Marple must suss out the culprit before they commit their next crime.

“As a reader of murder mysteries, I love this sense of the past catching up with people and people not getting away with things when they shouldn’t,” Foley says. “But I also love this idea, chaos is then going to be resolved for you at the end. There’s a nice wrapping up and a nice sense of resolution. I think that can be quite soothing and satisfying in troubled times.”
It’s all set up in a prologue, which Foley says was the first scene she thought of when she started writing.
“The first scene that came to me was the gondola going up the mountain,” she says. “The set piece of someone getting into the gondola alive and well at the bottom, and being found dead at the top.”
Get a taste of the mystery below.
Read the Prologue of Lucy Foley’s ‘Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel’
The top of the Grand Alpine gondola
Swiss Alps, 1950

The gondola rises silently through the bank of clouds into the frozen world at the top of the mountain. It is a wonder of modern engineer-ing, gliding between stanchions drilled into ancient rock, the red lacquer of its body gaudy against the bleak palette of white and gray.

There’s someone in the gondola. One of the hotel guests, most likely, eager to make the first tracks of the day. Fresh snow fell last night, leaving a pristine covering of powder over the mountain and softening the glacier that sweeps down one side. In the early morning light, it gives off a nacreous glow. Faint bluish indentations on the surface whisper of hidden, lethal chasms beneath.

In the tiny cabin beside the lift the attendant stamps his feet in his boots, blows on his hands to keep warm. He’s looking forward to interacting with another human being, however briefly. It’s a lonely existence up here with only the eagles for company, the only sounds the otherworldly groaning and cracking of the glacial ice as it con-tinues its endless creep toward the town. He knows the fears of his ancestors, how they believed in malign mountain spirits and giants living among these peaks, why they shunned them as a place of dark magic. Sometimes—­ when the seracs fall with crashes that seem to echo infinitely among the surrounding rock, or when a winter storm crackles with purple lightning, or when the low growl of an avalanche sounds at a distance—­ he’s not completely sure he doesn’t believe in such things himself.

The shadowy figure in the gondola sits with their head thrown back against the rear window; perhaps in awestruck appreciation of the view. The mechanism grinds to a halt. The doors begin to open. The seated figure does not move.

The attendant peers through the cabin window. Are they asleep? Are they not intending to get out? Perhaps they’ve come up here for the sights and will simply stay put and travel back the way they’ve come. More snow is on the way, after all: a great deal of it.
And yet . . . there’s something odd. A peculiar stillness about the scene. The attendant feels that he is just as alone as he was before the gondola and its occupant emerged through the clouds.
Should he go and see?
He doesn’t want to see.
He’s struck by the sudden impulse (odd; he’s a good Swiss Prot-estant) to cross himself.

Just as he steps out of his cabin into the freezing air the gondola gives the mechanical shudder that locks it into the final position. This is when the seated figure falls, stiff and inert as a Dresden doll knocked from a mantelpiece, keeling face-­ first onto the metal floor of the cabin.
For a moment the attendant watches in horror. Then he springs into action. But he knows, even as he hastens along the ice-­ slick path, that it is no use. The gondola’s passenger is already dead.

title: ‘The Traitors’ Cast Just Dropped, and it Features a ‘Love Island’ Narrator, a Former ‘Bachelor’ and Glinda the Good Witch
